Not surprising. Penny’s emotional responses originate from the primitive portion of the brain known as the Amygdala, while speech is centred in the much more recently developed Neocortex. The former can easily overpower the latter giving scientific credence to the notion of being rendered speechless. (Leonard stares at him.) Or maybe she just doesn’t want to talk.
Hey, look, I found an iPod.

Apparently he posted intimate details of their physical relationship on his blog, which I cannot find anywhere.
You know what, I’m going to go back and try talking to her again.
Good idea. Sit with her, hold her, comfort her, and if the moment feels right, see if you can cop a feel.

I’m not aware of any social convention that requires you to intervene at all.
What about “damsel in distress?”
Twelfth century code of chivalry, not exactly current. You’d also have to be knighted for that to apply.
I don’t care. She’s upset, I’m going over there.
Remember to sit on your hands a bit so they’re warm.
I’m her friend, I’m not going to take advantage of her vulnerability.
What, so you’re saying that if in the depths of despair she throws herself at you and demands you take her, right there, right now, you’ll just walk away?
I said I’m her friend. Not her gay friend.
Penny’s flat. Penny is eating ice cream from the tub.
Hey, listen, I know you said that you didn’t want to talk…
I don’t.
Sorry.
Wait.
Wait, did you say wait?
Tell me the truth. Am I just an idiot who picks giant losers?
No. No.
Okay, so I pick good guys, but turn them into losers.
Of course not.
Well, it’s got to be one or the other, which is it?
I’m sorry, what were the choices again?
I really thought Mike was different, I thought he was sensitive and smart. I mean, not you smart, normal non-freaky smart.
Yeah, no, sure.
You know, and then he just goes and has to humiliate me by writing about me on his blog so the entire world can read it.
Actually it’s not all that easy to find.
Yeah, really, well my friends at work found it, my sister found it, judging by my email a number of prisoners at the Michigan State Penitentiary found it.
Okay, well, what exactly did this guy write, not that I need to know the details of your sex life, I just thought…. never mind.
Nope, you know what, you might as well read it, everybody else has, go ahead. Oh God, I just feel so betrayed and embarrassed. I just want to crawl into a hole and die.
Okay, well, you know, this isn’t that bad. It just paints the picture of a very affectionate woman who’s open to expressing her affection in non traditional locales.
Oh God!
Elevators, parks, movie theatres, out of curiosity, is this subway the transportation system or subway the sandwich shop?
Sandwich shop.
Doesn’t that violate the health code?
No, at the sub shop we were only making out.
Huh. Okay. But my point is that you have absolutely no reason to be embarrassed.
Really, do you think I overreacted?
Maybe a little.
‘Cause I do that, I do overreact. Maybe I should call Mike and apologise.
No. No, no, that, that would be underreacting. He did break the implied confidentiality of the bedroom and, in your case, the elevator, parks and fast food franchise.
Yes. You’re right. I should just say I’m done with him.
Yes, you should, go ahead, say it.
But I never gave the man a chance to explain.
What is there to explain, it’s all right here, it’s a betrayal.
No, you were right the first time, this is a man who loves me, but in his own stupid way he was just trying to show people how he feels.
I’m pretty sure I never said that.
No, you did better than that, you helped me see it on my own.
Aw, good for me. Where are you going?
I’m going over to Mike’s. Leonard, thank you so much.
Oh, sure. Huh, maybe I am her gay friend.
The apartment. The guys are playing a board game and eating Chinese food.
Howard, I’m going to need another Mandarin lesson. I obviously didn’t make my point with those people.
For God’s sake, Sheldon, if you don’t like the tangerine chicken, don’t order the tangerine chicken.
I like tangerine chicken, I’m not getting tangerine chicken.
Can we please change the subject.
Sure. Tell us again how you screwed up and got Penny back together with her old boyfriend.
Just roll the dice.
Enslaved by warlocks, stay here till you roll 2, 4 or 6…7
She was mad at him. She was done with him, the relationship was broken beyond repair and I walked over there and I fixed it!
Boy, that story gets better every time you hear it.
Actually, I thought the first two renditions were far more compelling. Previously I felt sympathy for the Leonard character, now I just find him to be whiny and annoying.
Just eat your tangerine chicken.
I’d love to, but I don’t have tangerine chicken.
Thank you so much for your stupid advice. (Slams door again.)
Incredible. You managed to screw up the screw-up.
Penny’s apartment.
I’m back.

What happened?

Yeah, I know, I know that part.

Already, that was quick.
That’s what I said to the woman who had her legs wrapped around his neck.
Oh, Penny, I am so sorry.
How could he do that.
Oh, well, you know, you did throw an 8 gig iPod… yeah, no, how could he do that.
I swear to God, I am done with guys like that. You know, macho, with the perfect body and the hair, and the money.

What about me?
What about you what?

Are you asking me out?

Wow.

…thing and honest but, it’s no big deal…
Yes.
Yes what?
Yes, I will go out with you.
Really?

Yeah. That’s the spirit.
The lobby. Sheldon is listening to an iPod.
Show me your citrus peels. Gei wo kan, ni jud di zi pei. Show me your citrus peels. Gei wo kan, ni jud di zi pei. Show me your…
Sheldon.
Aieee ya! Xia si wo le.
I’m sorry. Look, do you have a second.
A second what? Pair of underwear?

Why me? Why not Koothrappali or Wolowitz?

Yes, I suppose he is.
All I’m saying is, you know Leonard the best.

Not necessarily. I’m often surprised by my lack of familiarity with Leonard. Just the other day I discovered, he not only has a loofah, he hides it. Why do you suppose a man would be ashamed of having a loofah? I myself prefer to have my excess epithelial cells slough off naturally, but I don’t condemn those who seek to accelerate the process.  (Time shift) And until recently I had no idea that despite his lactose intolerance, he can tolerate small amounts of non-fat ice cream without producing a noxious gas that I maintain in the right concentration could be weaponised. (Begins to unlock apartment door.)

We’re not done?
No.

Well, choose.
There are a number of options and, I’m really not familiar enough with the cushion densities, air flow patterns and dispersion of sunlight to make an informed choice.
Alright, why don’t you just pick one at random, and then if you don’t like it you can sit somewhere else next time.
No, no, that’s crazy. You go ahead and talk while I figure it out.

A little crush? Well I suppose so, in the same way Menelaus had a little crush on Helen of Troy.
Alright, yeah, I don’t really know who they are…
Well Menelaus was the brother of Agamemnon…
Yeah, I don’t care, I don’t care. The point is Leonard isn’t the kind of guy I usually go out with.
Leonard isn’t the kind of guy anyone usually goes out with. Would you be open to rotating the couch clockwise thirty degrees?
No. What I’m saying is, Leonard might be different in a good way. Obviously my usual choices have not worked out so well.
The last one worked out well for Koothrappali. He got a free iPod. Oh, glare!

But on the other hand, if things don’t go well with Leonard, I risk losing a really good friend. I mean, I guess he’s not looking for a fling, he’s the kind of guy that gets into a relationship for, I don’t know, like you would say light years.
I would not say that. No-one would say that, a light year is a unit of distance, not time.
Thank you for the clarification.
Draft. You see people hear the word year and they think duration. Foot pound has the same problem, that’s a unit of work, not of weight.
Right, thanks.
It’s a common mistake.
Not the first one I’ve made today.
Okay. I think this will be my seat.
Sheldon, do you have anything to say that has anything to do with, you know, what I’m talking about.
Well, let’s see. We might consider Schrodinger’s Cat.
Schrodinger? Is that the woman in 2A?
No. That’s Mrs Grossinger. And she doesn’t have a cat, she has a Mexican hairless, annoying little animal, yip yip yip yip…
Sheldon!

Sorry, you diverted me. Now, since no-one knows when or if the poison has been released, until the box is opened, the cat can be thought of as both alive and dead.

Well of course you don’t get it, I haven’t made it yet. You’d have to be psychic to get it, and there’s no such thing as psychic.

Just like Schrodinger’s Cat, your potential relationship with Leonard right now can be thought of as both good and bad. It is only by opening the box that you’ll find out which it is.
Okay, so you’re saying I should go out with Leonard.
No, no, no, no, no, no. Let me start again. In 1935, Erwin Schrodinger…
The University cafeteria.
Two seats right there.
Chong sho sha pwe. (Caption translates to “Long Live Concrete”.) Xie xie. (Thank you)
Sheldon, I think I’ve made a mistake.
I can see that. Unless you’re planning on running a marathon, choosing both stuffing and mashed potatoes is a starch filled redundancy.

Other people might be interested.

I assumed you would.

Right.
You also made a common grammatical mistake, you said nauseous when you meant nauseated. But go on.

Well, if we accept your premise, and also accept the highly improbable assumption that Penny is the only woman in the world for you then we can logically conclude that the result of blowing it would be that you end up a lonely, bitter old man with no progeny. Tell me whether or not to go through with the date.
Schrodinger’s Cat.
Wow, that’s brilliant.

Hi.
come on in.

I made an eight o’clock reservation.
Okay, great, listen, um, maybe we should talk first.

Show me your mucus! Your mucus!

This is not a tangerine bicycle.

dialogue: Oh Sheldon, please, look, I’m asking you as a friend.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: So you’re saying that friendship contains within it an inherent obligation to maintain confidences?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Well, yeah.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Interesting. See, one more question, and perhaps I should have led with this, when did we become friends?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: The stairwell.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I.e, I couldn’t become Green Lantern unless I was chosen by the guardians of Oa, but given enough start-up capital and an adequate research facility, I could be Batman.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: You could be Batman?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Sure. (In a gravelly voice) I’m Batman. See.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Hi guys.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Hey.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Hi Penny.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Hey, Penny, if you’re not doing anything Friday night I thought maybe we could go and see a movie.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Oh, um, you know, I think I have the dinner shift on Friday.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: What about Saturday?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: You know, I’m not sure, the manager hasn’t posted the schedule yet, how about I let you know.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Great. So you just let me know when you know. So… (she leaves) Oh God, I am the bad fish! What did I do wrong?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Why are you asking me, I have no information about your interactions with Penny other than what you provided me, nor do I have any method of learning such things. (Runs away.)

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: What does that mean?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Nothing. You seem to be implying an informational back channel between me and Penny where obviously none exists.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: No I didn’t.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I just think you need to be careful how you phrase things, sir.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: What’s going on with you?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Well I might ask you the same question. Why do you insist on attempting to drag me into matters which have nothing to do with me? But exist between you and Penny. A person to whom I barely speak. (His eye begins to twitch.)

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: What’s wrong with your face?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: There’s no reason to bring my looks into this. Good day, Leonard.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: What?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I said Good Day! (He leaves)

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Good day?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: The Cheesecake Factory

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Also today we have a fresh caught Alaska salmon, and that’s served with a teriyaki glaze and sticky rice. Our soup of the day…

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: You must release me from my oath.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Sheldon, I’m working.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Why don’t you take a minute to decide (leads her away) I can’t keep your secret Penny. I’m going to fold like an energy based anobo protein in conformational space. Like a renaissance triptych. Like a cheap suit.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Oh, look, why is it so hard for you to keep one little secret?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I’m constitutionally incapable. That’s why I was refused clearance for a very prestigious government research fellowship at a secret military supercollider, located beneath a fake agricultural station 12.5 miles south east of Travers City, Michigan. Which you did not hear about from me.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Look, just forget I told you about me not graduating from community college. Okay?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Forget! You want me to forget? This mind does not forget. I haven’t forgotten a single thing since the day my mother stopped breast feeding me. It was a drizzly Tuesday.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Okay, look, you promised me you would keep my secret so you’re just going to have to figure out a way to do it.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: The apartment.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Leonard, I’m moving out.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: What do you mean, you’re moving out? Why?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: There doesn’t have to be a reason.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Yeah, there kind of does.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Not necessarily. This is a classic example of munchausen’s trilemma. Either the reason is predicated on a series of sub-reasons leading to an infinite regression, or it tracks back to arbitrary axiomatic statements, or it’s ultimately circular, i.e., I’m moving out because I’m moving out.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I’m still confused.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Leonard, I don’t see how I could have made it any simpler.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Hey, qu’est q’wass up?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: We just got back from that exhibit of those plasticised human cadavers.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: And some of those skinless chicks were hot.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: If you’ll excuse me, I’m going to pack.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: That’s kind of an overreaction to a little harmless necrophilia.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: It’s not you, Howard, he says he’s moving out.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: What did you do? Did you change the contrast or brightness settings on the television?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: No.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Did you take a band aid off in front of him?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: No.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Did you buy generic ketchup, forget to rinse the sink, talk to him through the bathroom door?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Adjust the thermostat, cook with cilantro, pronounce the T in often?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: No.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Did you make fun of trains?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I didn’t do anything, he’s just gone insane.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Well, we all knew this day was coming.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: That was fast.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: It’s my pre-packed disaster evacuation bag. Recommended by the department of homeland security. And Sarah Connor.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Where are you gonna live?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Until I find a permanent place I will stay with friends.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Bye (runs out.)

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Well you can’t stay with me, I have a teeny tiny apartment.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Excuse me, but isn’t hosting guests an aspect of Menushya Yajna, one of the five central religious duties or sacrifices of the Hindu householder?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I hate trains.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Don’t be ridiculous, you love trains.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Yes I do, come on. See you later Leonard. (Sheldon drops keys in bowl and leaves without a word.)

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: This could work.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Raj’s apartment.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: This is a very old building.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Sixty years. Used to be a watch factory.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Uh-oh.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: What?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Don’t you worry about the residual radium from the luminous dials?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Not until now.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I can’t believe I didn’t bring my gieger counter. You know, I had it on my bed and I didn’t pack it.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Well, if you’re not comfortable staying here, Sheldon…

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I’m kidding, I packed it. It was a joke, I was subverting the conversational expectations. I believe they call that the, um, old switcheroo.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Terrific.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Is that woman Aishwarya Rai?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Yes, isn’t she an amazing actress.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Actually, I’d say she’s a poor man’s Madhuri Dixit.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: How dare you. Aishwarya Rai is a Goddess. By comparison Madhuri Dixit is a leprous prostitute.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Sorry, I didn’t mean to offend you. Obviously you’re not that familiar with Indian cinema.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Howard’s house. The door rings.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Who is it?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Strippergram. (Howard opens door. Outside are Raj and Sheldon.)

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Tag. You’re it. (Runs away.)

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Shouldn’t you have put him in a brown paper bag and set him on fire?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Howard’s bedroom. Howard is in bed, Sheldon is on a blow up mattress on the floor.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I’ve never slept on an air mattress before. No lumbar support whatsoever.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Maybe you’d be happier on a park bench?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I don’t see any way to get a park bench in here.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Do you want to switch?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: No, that’s fine. I’m perfectly comfortable sleeping on a bouncy castle.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Get out of bed, we’re switching.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Now, only if you want to.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Just get in the bed!

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: What’s going on? Are you boys roughhousing?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: We’re just talking ma.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: If you don’t settle down right now, I’m not going to let you have any more sleepovers.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: For God’s sake, ma, I’m 27 years old. It’s not even a school night! (To Sheldon) Comfy now?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Meh. That poster of Halle Berry’s a little unnerving.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: So don’t look at it.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: She’s like my fourth favourite catwoman.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: No kidding?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Yeah, Julie Newmar, Michelle Pfieffer, Eartha Kitt and then her.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: What about Lee Meriwether?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Oh, I forgot about Lee Meriwether.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Well I’m glad that’s settled.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: That makes Halle Berry my fifth favourite catwoman. There’s Julie Newmar, Michelle Pfieffer, Eartha Kitt, Lee Meriwether…

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Please, I’m begging you, go to sleep.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I’m trying, I’m counting catwomen. She did make a fine mutant in the X-Men movies though.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Oh for God’s sake.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: But she’s not my favourite of the X-Men, in order that would be Wolverine, Cyclops, oh wait, I forgot Professor X. Professor X, Wolverine, Cyclops, Iceman, then Storm, Angel, the Beast, oh wait, Nightcrawler. Professor X, Nightcrawler, Wolverine, Cyclops, Iceman, then Storm, Angel….

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Sheldon and Leonard’s apartment. There is an urgent rapping at the door.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I’m coming! (Opens the door. Sheldon falls inside, wearing his pyjamas. Howard is outside.)

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Hey, there he is, there’s my old buddy-bud-bud.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: What’s with him?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Koothrappali dumped him on me, and he couldn’t get to sleep, so I gave him a glass of warm milk with a handful of my mom’s valium in it. But he still wouldn’t shut up, so, tag, you’re it.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I’m ba-ack!

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I still don’t know why you left.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I can’t tell you.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Why not.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I promised Penny.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: You promised Penny what?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: That I wouldn’t tell you the secret. Shhhhh!

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: What secret. Tell me the secret.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Mom smokes in the car. Jesus is okay with it, but we can’t tell Dad.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Not that secret, the other secret.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I’m Batman. Shhhhh!

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Dammit, Sheldon! You said Penny told you a secret, what was the secret.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Okay, I’ll tell you, but you can’t tell Leonard.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I promise.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Penny lied about graduating from community college because she is afraid she’s not smart enough for Leonard.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: So it’s nothing I did? It’s her problem?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I drank milk that tasted funny.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Penny thinks I’m too smart for her, that’s ridiculous.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: I know, most of your work is extremely derivative. Don’t worry, that’s not a secret. Everybody knows.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: The hallway. Leonard is outside Penny’s door.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Hi.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Yeah, hi, listen, I know what’s been bothering you about us, and I have the answer.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: What are you talking about.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: First I want to say that it’s not Sheldon’s fault, he tried very hard to keep your secret, if Howard hadn’t drugged him he would have taken it to his grave.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: He told you?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Yes, but it’s okay. Now that we know what the problem is, there’s a simple solution. (Hands her a brochure.)

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Pasadena city college?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: A place for fun, a place for knowledge. See, this man here’s playing hacky sack, and this girl’s going to be a paralegal.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Wow, I get it, because Dr Leonard Hofstadter can’t date a girl without a fancy college degree.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Well, it’s really not that fancy, it’s just a city college.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Right, but I have to have some sort of degree to date you?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: That doesn’t matter to me at all.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: So, it’s fine with you if I’m not smart.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 01 – The Bad Fish Paradigm
dialogue: Absolutely. (She slams the door in his face.) Okay, this time I know where I went wrong. (Looking up and seeing the camera) Oh bite me!
The building entrance lobby. The guys enter. Sheldon is dressed as a medieval monk, Howard is a court jester, Raj is a medieval gentleman and Leonard is a knight.
Worst Renaissance Fair ever.
Please let it go, Sheldon.

It was rife with historical inaccuracies. For example, the tavern girl serving flagons of mead, now her costume was obviously Germanic, but in 1487 the Bavarian purity laws or Rhineheitsgebot severely limited the availability of mead. At best they would have had some sort of spiced wine.
You’re nitpicking.
Oh-ho! Really? Well here’s another nit for you. The flagons would not have been made of polypropylene.
Renaissance fairs aren’t about historical accuracy. They’re about taking chubby girls who work at Kinko’s and lacing them up in corsets so tight their bosom jumps out and says howdy.
Bosoms would not have said howdy in the fifteenth century. If anything they would have said “huzzah!”
I don’t care what the bosoms say, Sheldon, I just want to be part of the conversation.
Hi guys. Looks like you’ve been to the Renaissance fair. I’m hoping.
Renaissance fair? More of a medieval slash age of enlightenment slash any excuse to wear a codpiece fair.
Okay, fine, whatever, um, you guys, this is my friend Eric.
Hello.
Hi.
Hey.
So, yeah, good to see you.
Yeah, yeah, it’s good to see you too. We should really go.
Yeah.
Bye guys.
Like your hat.
Thanks, my mom made it. Penny with a new guy, tres awkward.
It wasn’t awkward. It wasn’t fun. Besides, what’s the big deal, we dated, we stopped dating, and now we’re both moving on.
By moving on, do you mean, she’s going out with other men and you spent the afternoon making fifteenth century soap with Wolowitz?
That was not fifteenth century soap, my God those people need to learn you can’t just put “ye olde” in front of anything and expect to get away with it.
Can we please just go in, my chain mail is stuck in my underwear.
You’re wearing modern underwear?
Relatively modern. Why, what are you wearing?
I fashioned historically accurate undergarments out of linen.
You went out and bought linen?
Don’t be silly, I borrowed one of your pillow cases.
Borrowed?
The apartment.
You know what, I’m happy that Penny’s moving on. It gives me the freedom to move on myself.
Are you saying that you’ve been holding back?
Of course. Out of respect.
So, how do you explain the ten years before Penny?
Who were you respecting then?
What? I’ve dated plenty of women. There was Joyce Kim, Leslie Winkle.
Notify the editors of the Oxford English Dictionary, the word plenty has been redefined to mean two.
Uh, what about that girl last year at Comic-con?
Doesn’t count.
Why not?
What happens in costume at Comic-con, stays at Comic-con.
You’re only saying that because of what happened to you.
What happened to you?
N-n-n-nothing happened to me.
It wasn’t your fault, Raj, he was dressed as a green Orion slave girl.
H-h-h-how did we get on me, we were mocking Leonard for not moving on. Dude, you have totally not moved on.
Yes I have, it’s just a matter of actually making a date with someone.
Like who?
Well, there’s Joyce Kim, but she defected back to North Korea so it’s a little geographically undesireable.
What about Leslie Winkle.
Oh no.
Why?
Her research methodology is sloppy, she’s unjustifiably arrogant about loop quantum gravity, and to make matters worse she’s often mean to me.
I think she’s smoking hot.
I’d hit that.
You’d hit particulate soil on a colloidal suspension. Mud.
Look, I like Leslie, but she’s not interested in dating as much as using men as tools for stress release.
Yeah, so, be a tool. Go get yourself a little rebound stress release.
Technically it would only be rebound if he and Penny had actually engaged in physical intimacy.
You mean like you and Richard the slave girl?
I bought him dinner and we kissed once, that was it. (Leaving) And he told me his name was Kimberley!
The university cafeteria.
You know how I know we’re not in The Matrix?
How?
If we were, the food would be better.
Hey, Leonard.
Hey, Leslie.
Hey, dummy.
Hello to you, insufficiently intelligent person.
Ooh, rush me to the burn unit. Hey, Leonard, do you have a second, I need to ask you something.
Uh, sure.
Well, if you’ll excuse me, I’m going to go do work that promises significant results, as opposed to what you do, which does not. Yeah, you heard me.
Wow. So, I heard your relationship with Penny crashed to the ground like blue ice falling out of an airplane lavatory.
Where did you hear that?
Actually I read it. Wolowitz texted me. (Shows him text.)
Like blue ice falling out of an airplane lavatory. Yep.
I thought it was a pretty good one, I gave him an L-O-L. Anyway, it got me thinking, now that you’re unattached maybe we can revisit our previous attachment.
Are you suggesting another bout of stress release.
No, I’m all done with casual sex. From now on I’m fully committed to the traditional relationship paradigm.
Really, what changed?
It’s hard to say, I guess there’s just a time in every woman’s life when she gets tired of waking up on a strange futon with a bunch of people she doesn’t know.
Yeah, I can see how that would… a bunch of people?
Anyway, I just figure it’s time to slow things down and who better to slow things down with than you?
Oh, I’m flattered. So, how do you suggest we proceed?
Your place, we’ll order Chinese, you’ll rent a movie, artsy but accessible, then light petting, no coitus.
Sounds fun.
I’ll leave the details up to you, I think it’s better if you assume the male role.
Thank you, that’s very thoughtful.
Great. Call me.
The apartment. Leonard is dressed smartly and placing wine on the table. Sheldon enters.
Great news. My mom sent me my old Nintendo 64.
Terrific.
You know what this means, don’t you? Break out the Red Bull, it’s time to rock Mario old school.
I kind of have other plans tonight.
But it’s Friday. Friday’s always vintage game night. Look, mom included the memory card, we can pick up where I left off in 1999 when I had pernicious anaemia.
Well, the thing is, someone’s coming over.
Well then, no problem, I have three controllers, the more the merrier.
Sheldon, it’s a date, I have a date coming over.
Oh, well you can’t blame me for not jumping to that conclusion.

The university cafeteria.

So, dumbass, I heard you made a grad student throw up last night.

Excuse me, Dr. Cooper, I’m Ramona Nowitzki, I was at your talk last night. I think you’re just brilliant.
That is the prevailing opinion.
Oh, now I’m gonna throw up.
Howard Wolowitz, department of engineering, co-designer of the International Space Station’s Liquid Waste Disposal System.

Ew. Dr. Cooper, I’ve read everything you’ve published. I especially liked your paper on grand unification using string-network condensates and was wondering how you determined that three-dimensional string-nets provided a unified picture of fermions and gauge bosons?

Excuse me?

You got it. I already have your address.

I’m sorry?
I believe one day Sheldon will eat an enormous amount of Thai food and split into two Sheldons.

Drat.

Godzilla clause?

Sisters?

The university cafeteria
Mmm, gentlemen, I put it to you, the worst tapioca pudding is better than the best pudding of any other flavour.
First off, that is axiomatically wrong, because the best pudding is chocolate. Secondly, the organic structure of tapioca makes it a jiggling bowl of potential death. It is extracted from the plant…

It is extracted from the plant…

Really? I once saw him shopping at Ralph’s. He was buying tequila.

Alright this is cruel, we better let him finish before his head explodes.
Alright Sheldon, why is tapioca…
Tapioca is extracted from the root of the plant Manihot Esculenta. Due to a high concentration of cyanide it is poisonous in its raw form and lethal if prepared improperly.
Feel better now?
It is also indigenous to Brazil, as is the Cocoa Bean, from which we get chocolate, the best pudding. And you promised you wouldn’t do that anymore!
Hey Hofstadter!
Hey Kripke.
Heard about your watest pwoton decay expewiment, twenty thousand data wuns and no statistically significant wesults. Vewy impwessive!
What a jerk.
Don’t feel bad Leonard, negative results are still results.
Even twenty thousand of ’em.
Alright, please don’t cheer me up anymore.
C’mon, don’t let him get to you. It’s Kripke.
Yeah, he’s a ginormous knob.
That’s why he eats by himself, instead of sitting here at the cool table.
Fo’ shizzle.

Hey it’s true, Kripke lacks the basic social skills that we take for granted, but he also controls the new open science grid computer that I need to use to run some simulations of structure formation in the early universe.
Good luck getting time on it. The only people he lets use it are his friends.
Well then, the solution is simple. I shall befriend him. Kripke!
Yeah?
What’d you say of the idea of you and I becoming friends?
I would say, I have no intewest in becoming your fwiend.
Really? That seems rather short sighted, coming from someone who is generally considered altogether unlikable. Why don’t you take some time to reconsider?
Yeah, I’ll do that.
Well I think we’re off to a terrific start.
The apartment.
There you go. Now any e-mail from Wolowitz will go right into your spam folder.
Thanks! I mean the e-mail doesn’t bother me as much as the vacation pictures of him in a bathing suit.
Yeah, I got the same one. And that’s not a bathing suit, it’s a tan line.

Hello. This is Sheldon Cooper. I’m leaving a message for Barry Kripke. Barry, It was pleasant seeing you today in the cafeteria. I saw that you purchased the chef’s salad. Apparently, you did not know that the chef’s salad is kitchen trickery, to utilize scrap meat. Nevertheless, I hope you enjoyed it. I’m following up on our pending friendship, and I look forward to hearing from you regarding its status. Sheldon Cooper.
What’s up with Ichabod?
Oh he’s trying to make a new friend.
Oh really? Well, good for him.
Well, unless he’s makes one out of wood like Gepetto, I don’t think it’s gonna happen.
Well, how did you guys become friends?
There was a flier on the bulletin board at the university. Roommate wanted. Whistlers need not apply.
And you moved in anyway?
I assumed he was joking. You’d be surprised how many particle physicists have a whimsical side.
Well, what about Howard and Raj, I mean how did you become friends with them?
I don’t know, how do carbon atoms form a benzene ring? Proximity and valence electrons.
Well yeah, sure. When you put it that way. But it all worked out, right?
I suppose. I do miss whistling though.
Oh come on, really? (Leonard whistles)
First warning.
Outside Penny’s door.
Hello Sheldon.
Hi.
What is this?
It’s a questionnaire I devised. I’m having some difficulty bonding with a colleague at work, so I’m doing a little research to better understand why my current friends like me.
Yes. Well, that is a good question. But is this really the best way to figure it out?
Yeah, I agree, the social sciences are largely hokum. But, short of putting electrodes in your brain and monitoring your response to my companionship, this is the best I can do.
Okay, question 1. Rank the following aspects of Sheldon Cooper in order of appeal. Intelligence. Ruthless attention to hygiene. Playfulness. Java applet writing?

I know, I may have started off with a fairly obvious one. You did an aspect of my most appealing trait, playfulness. Why don’t you just go ahead and write that number 1. I’m afraid you’re on your own for the rest. It should take you no more than 3 hours.
Wait! How many questions are on this thing?
Only 211. Don’t worry, in deference to you, I’ve kept them on a high school graduate reading level.
Thanks pal.
You got it, buddy.
Sheldon honey, did you ever consider making friends by being, I don’t know, pleasant?
Well that’s certainly a thought-provoking hypothesis. May I suggest it as the topic for your essay.
The apartment. Sheldon is reading one of the questionnaires. He tuts.
Your questionnaire, very disappointing.
I answered every question Sheldon.
You answered the multiple choice questions in a pattern. A B B A C. A B B A C.
Aw, you picked up on that huh?
How could I not?
Come on! There’s over 200 questions. And look at some of these things. Sheldon is to camaraderie, as the space shuttle is to blank?

There are a number of acceptable answers, for example, C: near earth transport, but certainly not B: avocado rancher. And your essay, suggesting that I’d have better luck making friends if I wait ’til the Cylons take over? Please.

What hope do I have for establishing new relationships given that my current friends apparently cannot take a few hours out of their lives to help me?
Sheldon, I’m not going to defend a big-balled raccoon.
I don’t see how you could.
What I’m trying to say is that, maybe you can’t approach this as a purely intellectual exercise.
What do you mean!?
Well, remember when you tried to learn how to swim using the internet?
I did learn how to swim.
On the floor.
The skills are transferrable. I just have no interest in going in the water.

The ice caps are melting Leonard. In the future, swimming isn’t going to be optional. But you do bring up an interesting point. I don’t have to break new ground here, I’m sure much of the research already exists.
No! no, my point is, if you want to learn how to make friends, then just go out to a coffee shop or a museum. Meet people. Talk to them. Take an interest in their lives.

A bookshop.
Coping with the death of a loved one. My condolences.
Thank you.
Family or friend?
Family.

I assume the skills can be extrapolated and transferred.

Oh my! That’s awfully sticky. Alright, let’s see. Bernie Bunny has Two Daddies Now. It’s probably about homosexual rabbits. Jerry the Gerbil and the Bullies on the Bus. Read it, not helpful. Oh! See, my initial approach to Kripke, had the same deficiencies as those that plagued Stu the Cockatoo, when he was new at the zoo.
Stu the cockatoo?

Alright Kripke, that last interest strikes me as the least objectionable and I would like to propose that we do that together. Tomorrow. Yes, I’ll pay. Alright, goodbye. Alright! Time to learn rock climbing.

Sheldon, are you okay?

Me, me. Let it be me.
Leonard, you are my roommate, my source of transportation and you help me fold my sheets when they come out of the dryer. You are safe.
Can I whistle?

No. You, too, are safe.

Penny, Penny, Penny. Everything you’re saying is true, but please allow me to continue. Raj, you’re out. Unacceptable, the delay would result in tomorrow morning’s bowel movement occurring at work.

Wow. I don’t see how we missed that.

That’s how we missed it.
Sheldon, would you be prepared, on a non-precedential basis, to create an emergency ad-hoc Slurpie-Icee equivalency?

The hallway. Sheldon is opening the apartment door. Penny comes running up stairs.

Just do it! (Penny runs in. Sheldon shuts door. Penny opens door again) Get inside and shut the door.

The building manager’s showing an apartment downstairs, and I haven’t paid my rent.
Oh, I see. Penny, I’m not sure I’m comfortable harbouring a fugitive from the 2311 North Los Robles Corporation.
It’s no big deal. I’m just a little behind on my bills because they cut back my hours at the restaurant and my car broke down.
If you recall, I pointed out the “check engine” light to you several months ago.
Well the “check engine” light is fine. It’s still blinking away. It’s the stupid engine that stopped working. It cost me like twelve hundred dollars to fix it.
You know, it occurs to me you could solve all your problems by obtaining more money.
Yes, it occurs to me, too.
Hang on a moment. (He opens a jar. Snakes jump out. He then pulls out a large wedge of money) Here. Take some. Pay me back when you can.
Wow, you got a lot of money in there.
That’s why it’s guarded by snakes. Take some.
Don’t be silly.
I’m never silly. Here.
No, I can’t.
Don’t you need money?
Well, yeah, but…
This is money I’m not using.

My expenses account for 46.9% of my after-tax income. The rest is divvied up between a small savings account, this deceptive container of peanut brittle and the hollowed-out buttocks of a superhero action figure who shall remain nameless for his own protection. Or her own protection. Take some.

I see no large upcoming expenditures unless they develop an affordable technology to fuse my skeleton with adamantium like Wolverine.
Are they working on that?
I sincerely hope so.
Okay. Well, thank you. Oh, God, no, I can’t. Sheldon honey, I don’t want things to be weird between us.
Won’t it also be weird if I have to say hello to you every morning on my way to work and you’re living in a refrigerator box and washing your hair with rain water?
I’ll pay you back as soon as I can.
Of course you will. It’s impossible to pay me back sooner than you can. Assuming you subscribe to a linear understanding of time and causality.
I’m regretting this already.
Entering the lobby of the building.
You know, I’ve given the matter some thought, and I think I’d be willing to be a house pet to a race of super-intelligent aliens.
Interesting.
Ask me why.
Do I have to?

Why?

No.
Was that sarcasm?
Yes.
Was that sarca..

All right.

Weird.

The apartment

Sit on the damn couch.

More?

Golden Dragon.

The paint ball range.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Hey, you know what’d be a great idea? We get some girls over here and play Laser Obstacle Strip Chess.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Believe me, Howard, any girl who would be willing to play that, you don’t want to see naked.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: You underestimate me.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Outside Penny’s door. Sheldon stands looking at his watch with his hand poised to knock. At the right moment he starts knocking.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: (Knock, knock, knock) Penny, (knock, knock, knock) Penny, (knock, knock, knock) Penny.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Hey, Sheldon.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: It’s eleven am.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I know. You’re safe.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: This package came while you were at work.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Oh, great, my rhinestones. Thank you.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Excuse me.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: What?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: You have to sign this.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: What is it?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: When I signed for the package, I was deputized by the United Parcel Service and entrusted with its final delivery. I now need you to acknowledge receipt of the package so that I’m fully indemnified and no longer liable.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Sheldon, it’s just a box of rhinestones.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Well, the contents are irrelevant. A legal bailment has been created. Does that mean nothing to you?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: It means nothing to anybody. Come here, let me show you what I’m doing.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Bailment describes a relationship in common law where a physical possession of personal property, or chattels, is transferred from one person, the bailor, to another person, the bailee.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Look, look, look! I started a business.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Obviously, not a cleaning business.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: No, I’m making flower barrettes. See? I call them Penny Blossoms. I made one for myself, then all the girls at work wanted one. Then I showed some to this lady who runs a shop in Old Town. She sells cards and homemade jewellery. She said she wanted to sell them. I said okay, and in one week, I made a $156.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Good for you. Sign here.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Sheldon, don’t you get it? If this takes off, I won’t have to be a waitress anymore.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: But then who will bring me my cheeseburger on Tuesday nights?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Another waitress.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: What’s her name?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I don’t know.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: And you’re going to let her handle my food?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Nancy. Her name is Nancy.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I think you’re just making that up.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Sheldon, I’m sorry about your hamburger, okay? I just don’t want to be a waitress for the rest of my life.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Cheeseburger. I get a cheeseburger.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Fine, cheeseburger.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Maybe I’d be better off with Nancy.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: So, what do you think? I mean, this could be a business, right?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: How many of these can you make a day?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: About twenty.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: And how much profit do you make per Penny Blossom?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I don’t know, like, 50 cents. I’m not sure.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: No, Of course you’re not. All right, ten dollars a day times five days a week times 52 weeks a year is two thousand six hundred dollars.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: That’s all?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Before taxes.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Well, I don’t have to pay taxes on this stuff.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I believe the Internal Revenue Service would strongly disagree. But, if you took advantage of modern marketing techniques, and you optimized your manufacturing process, you might be able to make this a viable business.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: And you know about that stuff?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Penny, I’m a physicist. I have a working knowledge of the entire universe and everything it contains.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Who’s Radiohead?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I have a working knowledge of the important things in the universe. Good luck.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Sheldon, hold on. Could you maybe show me how to make more money with this?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Of course I could.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Sheldon, wait! Will you?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Just to be clear here, you’re asking for my assistance.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Yes.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: And you understand that will involve me telling you what to do?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I understand.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: And you’re not allowed to be sarcastic or snide to me while I’m doing so.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Okay.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Good. Let’s begin with the premise that everything you’ve done up to this point is wrong.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Oh, imagine that.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Sarcasm. Good-bye.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: No, sorry. Wait! Please come back!

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Penny’s apartment. Penny is making a barette. Sheldon is timing her.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: There. Done.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: All right. 12 minutes and 17 seconds.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Pretty good, right?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: That’s 4.9 Penny Blossoms per hour. Based on your cost of materials and your wholesale selling price, you’ll effectively be paying yourself… $5.19 a day.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: A day?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: There are children in a sneaker factory in Indonesia who outearn you.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: That just can’t be right.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: You’re questioning my math?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: No, sorry.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Want me to show my work?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Oh, God, no, no. Just please tell me what to do about it.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: All right, are you familiar with the development that resulted from Honoré Blanc’s 1778 use of interchangeable parts? The assembly line, of course.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Okay, you know what, if I’m not allowed to be snide, you’re not allowed to be condescending.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: That wasn’t a part of our original agreement, and I do not agree to it now.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: All right, fine. How are we supposed to set up machines and conveyor belts in my apartment?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: You’re thinking of the moving assembly line, an understandable but not excusable mistake. No. The moving assembly line, that was introduced by Henry Ford in 1908. That innovation is what made possible our modern consumer culture by enabling a low-unit cost for manufactured goods. I guess that isn’t one of the topics discussed on your Radiohead.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: The apartment

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Let’s go. We’re going to miss the coming attractions.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: What’s the matter?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I think I bruised a testicle capturing that last pawn.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Hello?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Hello. (They resume singing and working)

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: W-W-Wait, what’s going on?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I assume you’re referring to the sea shanty. It’s a rhythmic work song designed to increase productivity.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Yeah, it’s crazy, but it totally works. Look, we made this Penny Blossom in under three minutes.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Terrific, but that kind of raises more questions than it answers.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Penny’s making hair accessories. I’m helping her optimize her manufacturing process. All right, break’s over. (They start singing again.)

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Hold on. What are you using as a bonding agent?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Hot glue.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: You’re kidding. Any of the cyanoacrylates would do a better job.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: It won’t work, the flower’s too porous.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: What if we infused the bottom layer with silicone-RTV to provide a better mounting surface?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Intriguing.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Good question, what are you marketing and distribution channels?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Well, there are the waitresses at my work, and this cute, little shop in Old Town.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Hush, hush, hush, hush, hush, virtually non-existent. I’m thinking that we set her up with a hosted turnkey e-commerce system to start.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Why not eliminate the middle man? We could install a small server farm with a static IP in her bedroom.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: She’d need some kind of industrial cooling system.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Of course, but before we set up a marketing and distribution infrastructure, we should finish optimizing the manufacturing process. To start with, she has a terrible problem with moisture-induced glitter clump.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Yeah, it’s a bitch.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Uh, I’ve seen this before.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Where?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: It’s a common stripper problem. They dance, they sweat, they clump.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Ew.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Are you thinking about adding a desiccant like calcium sulphate?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Actually, I’m thinking about this one stripper named Vega. But sure, calcium sulphate could work.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Let’s think out of the box for a moment. How about a molecular sieve?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Oh!

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I’ve got a spaghetti strainer in the kitchen.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Wow.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Hey, we could liberate some micro-porous charcoal from the chem lab.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Oh, great. Raj, why don’t you and Howard go get the charcoal? Leonard, why don’t you start working on some preliminary Web site designs. I’ll make some space in our apartment so we can move the manufacturing process.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Well, what’s wrong with my apartment?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: It’s not my apartment.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Wait, wait, what am I going to do?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Uh, hey, it’s your business. Do whatever you want.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Oh, okay, cool. I’m going to take a nap.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: The apartment.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I’m still tweaking things a little bit, but this will give you the general idea of the Web site. So, what do you guys think?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Uh, pretty much any way I say that is going to hurt his feelings.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Okay, what’s wrong with it?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: – What’s wrong with it?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Not you. I wasn’t asking you. Penny?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Uh, well, it’s a little juvenile. I mean, it kind of looks like the MySpace page of a 13-year-old girl.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: No, it doesn’t.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Please. Dateline could use it to attract predators.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Penny, this is your enterprise, so it’s ultimately your decision, but based on the quality of his work, I’d strongly recommend that we let Leonard go.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: You want to fire me?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: What I want is irrelevant. This is Penny’s decision. Penny?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Excuse me, but if I did such a bad job then why do we already have orders?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: We do?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Uh-huh. Look. Mrs. Fiona Fondell from Huntsville, Alabama has ordered two.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: No kidding. Two?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Uh-huh. Look at the comments.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Thank you, Penny Blossoms. These will be perfect to cover my bald spot. Aww, that is so sweet.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Camouflaging bald spots. That’s primarily a male concern. Perhaps we could expand our market.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: How are flower barrettes going to appeal to men?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: We add Bluetooth!

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Brilliant. Men love Bluetooth.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Wait a minute, wait a minute, you want to make a hair barrette with Bluetooth?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Penny, everything is better with Bluetooth.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Holy crap. Someone just ordered a thousand Penny Blossoms.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Get out! Who needs a thousand sparkly flower barrettes with rhinestones?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: The Fifth Annual East Rutherford, New Jersey, Gay, Lesbian, Bisexual and Transgender Alliance Luau.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Oh, another market to expand into, balding gay men.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: And I’ll bet lesbians love Bluetooth.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: We should get to work.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Wait, wait, wait, why does it say one-day rush? Since when do we offer a one-day rush?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Amazon offers one-day rush.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Yeah, but they don’t have to glue the books together. How the hell are we going to make a thousand Penny Blossoms in one day?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Don’t yell at me. I’m not manufacturing. I’m just Web design.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Okay, well, I’m gonna have to call them and cancel the order.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Excuse me, but was this not your goal? Financial independence through entrepreneurial brilliance and innovation? My brilliance and innovation, of course, but still.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I just don’t see how see can pull this off.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Okay, that, right there, that equivocation and self-doubt, that is not the American spirit. Did Davy Crockett quit at the Alamo? Did Jim Bowie?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: They didn’t quit. They were massacred by, like, a gazillion angry Mexicans.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Alright, let me put it this way. Your gross receipts on this one order will be over $3,000 for one night’s work.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: You guys get started.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: What are you doing?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Going online to buy shoes!

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: The same, later. Sheldon and Penny are making barettes, singing “She’ll be coming round the mountain.”

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: You know, if I wanted to spend my Saturday nights doing this, I could have stayed in India.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Oh, stop with the fake third world crap. Your father’s a gynaecologist, and you had a house full of servants.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: We only had four servants. And two of them were children.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: How are we doing?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: We have 128 assorted Penny Blossoms ready to ship.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Oh, God, we’re never gonna finish in time. Who made Sheldon the boss anyway?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I believe I’m hearing some negativity on the factory floor.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: So?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Penny, the labour force is a living organism that must be carefully nurtured. Any counterproductive grumbling must be skilfully headed off by management. Observe. Hey! Less talk, more work!

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Nicely done.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Thank you. You hear any union talk, you let me know.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Someone’s in the kitchen with Dinah…

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Someone’s in the kitchen I know-ow-ow-ow

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Someone’s in the kitchen with Dinah… Sheldon? Sheldon! (nudges him)

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: ‘Cause I sold my soul to the company store.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Honey, do you want some coffee?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: No, I don’t drink coffee.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Come on, but if you don’t stay awake we’ll never finish in time.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I’m sorry, coffee’s out of the question. When I moved to California, I promised my mother that I wouldn’t start doing drugs.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Leonard, help.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Sheldon, we still have 380 of these things to make.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I have complete faith that you will make them. Good night.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Leonard?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Yeah, no. But, Sheldon, without your insight and leadership this entire enterprise will surely fail.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: You’re right, of course.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Here, this will help.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Very well, but if this leads to opiates or hallucinogenics, you’re going to have to answer to my mother.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Look at Planck’s Constant. People say it’s arbitrary. It could not be less arbitrary. If it varied even slightly, life as we know it would not exist. Bam! Now, now, let’s reconsider the entire argument, but with entropy reversed and effect preceding cause, so you are thinking of a universe that’s not expanding from the centre, no, it is retreating from a, from a possibility space. Bam! This is a space where we are all essentially Alice through the looking glass, standing in front the Red Queen, and we’re being offered a cracker to quench our thirst. Bam! Of course, in another universe, let’s call it universe prime, there’s another Sheldon, let’s call him Sheldon prime…

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: We should have let him go to bed.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Bam.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I can’t believe we actually did it.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: 1,000 friggin’ Penny Blossoms.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I just want you guys to know I am really grateful for your help, and for every dollar I make, I’m going to give you 20 cents.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: That’s your entire profit margin.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: Oh. Then never mind.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: I’ll print out the shipping label. Uh-oh.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: What?

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster
dialogue: We got an e-mail from the East Rutherford, New Jersey, Gay, Lesbian, Bisexual and Transgender Alliance. They want another thousand Penny Blossoms.

episode_name: Series 02 Episode 18 – The Work Song Nanocluster

dialogue: Uh, Houston, this is more of an FYI call. We are basically out the door.
The apartment. Leonard is working on a whiteboard.
Oh, boy.
What?
I can’t comment without violating our agreement that I don’t criticize your work.
Then what was oh, boy?
Great restraint on my part.
There’s nothing wrong with the science here.
Perhaps you mean a different thing than I do when you say science.
Okay, how’s that?

You actually had it right in the first place. Once again, you’ve fallen for one of my classic pranks. Bazinga! Well, now here’s a peculiar e-mail. The president of the university wants me to meet him at his office tomorrow morning at 8 a.m.
Why?
It doesn’t say. It must be an emergency. Everyone at the university knows I eat breakfast at eight and move my bowels at 8:20.
Yes, how did we live before Twitter? I guess you’ll find out what it is in the morning.

That’s 14 hours away. For the next 840 minutes, I’m effectively one of Heisenberg’s particles, I know where I am or I know how fast I’m going, but I can’t know both. Yet how am I supposed to carry on with this huge annoying thing hovering over my head?
Yeah, I know the feeling.
Outside Leonard’s bedroom.
(Knock, knock, knock) Leonard. (Knock, knock, knock) Leonard. (Knock, knock, knock) Leonard.
Sheldon, it’s two o’clock in the morning.
Why is everybody keep telling me what time it is?
Everybody?
You, the president of the university, his wife, their sullen teenage daughter. That entire family is fascinated by what time it is and whether people know it.
You went to President Seibert’s house in the middle of the night?
He didn’t respond to my e-mail, his phone number is unlisted. Tell me what my other option was.
You could have waited until morning. I know, look who I’m talking to.
Do you remember the grant proposal I submitted to the National Science Foundation to detect slow-moving monopoles at the magnetic North Pole?
Hardly a day goes by when I don’t think about it.
Aw, how nice. Well, a space opened up at the last minute on the NSF expedition to the Arctic Circle.
Wait a minute. He offered to send you to the North Pole?
Yes. In fact, he was quite enthusiastic. He said, “Frankly, if I could send you tonight, I would.”
Okay, well, do you want to go?

Of course not. I’m a theoretical physicist, a career I chose in no small part because it’s indoors, but if I’m able to detect slow-moving magnetic monopoles there, I will be the scientist to confirm string theory. People will write books about me. Third-graders will create macaroni-art dioramas depicting scenes from my life.
Sure, maybe a tableau of me trying to pummel you to death.
Sarcasm?
Maybe.
I’m on the horns of a dilemma. Can you imagine me, Sheldon Cooper, at the North Pole?
Easy peasy, I’m doing it right now.
I’m not good with cold, Leonard. How often have we had to leave a movie theatre because I got a headache from drinking the Icee too fast? I can’t go.
Well, then don’t go.
How can you say that? The scientific opportunity of a lifetime presents itself and my best friend says don’t go.
All right, then go.
Listen to you. How can I possibly go?
Sheldon, what are the words I can say right now to end this conversation and let me go back to sleep?
Odd, President Seibert posed the exact same question.
How was it resolved?
It wasn’t. His wife set their dogs on me and rendered the question moot.
The stairwell.
Just imagine. If he says yes, we’ll have an entire summer without Sheldon.
We could play outside.
We could sit on the left side of the couch.
I could use the bathroom at 8:20.
Our dreams are very small, aren’t they?
Good news, gentlemen, I have tentatively accepted…

…the invitation to join the Arctic Expedition.
It’s not gonna be the same without you.
Godspeed.
Thank you, but your sentiments may be premature.
Ooh, I don’t like where this is going.
I would like to propose that the three of you accompany me.
To the North Pole?
Yes.
Is this just so we won’t touch your stuff while you’re away?
I’ll admit that was a concern. But the fact is, I’ll need a support team. And the three of you are my first choice.
Really?

Well, there are others who might be more qualified, but the thought of interviewing them gave me a stomach ache. Now, I know I’m proposing an enormous undertaking, so why don’t you take a few moments to discuss it?
We’re not really gonna go to the North Pole with him, are we?
I’m still within earshot! You may want to wait for my door to close.
We’re not really gonna go to the North Pole with him, are we?
