episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Sheldon, what is wrong with you?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Not much. Although, I can be faulted for being overly fond of koala bears. I don’t know what it is, when they smart munching on eucalyptus, I just melt inside.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Okay, Amy just told you some exciting news, and you acted like it was no big deal.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Oh, I see why you’re confused. No, her news sounded important, but what you’re forgetting is, it was an achievement in the field of biology. That’s all about yucky, squishy things.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Honey, she’s upset. You’re her boyfriend. You have to at least try to be excited by the things she’s excited by.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: What if they simply don’t excite me?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Well, just smile and think about koalas.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: She’d see right through that. We go to the zoo all the time. She knows my koala face. And for future reference, it’s this.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Howard’s bedroom.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Oh, you have a lot of magic stuff.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Yeah. I started when I was a teenager. I thought I could show a girl a few tricks and invite her up to my bedroom to see the rest of the act.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Did it work?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Ah, let’s just say the only wand that ever saw any action was this one. Oh, look what my mom made us for the act.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Ooh. I like the fabric. Where’d she get it?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Well, she cut up one of her old bathing suits. She made these two vests and half a dozen napkins.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Has she tried on the vest yet?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I just gave it to her!

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I hope it fits, she has a tricky figure! She’s short and stacked, like me!

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: She’s not stacked like you, Ma! She never steps on hers!

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Listen, Howie, maybe I’m not the best choice to be a magician’s assistant.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: You’ll do fine. Hand me those rings? See? You nailed it.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: You know, i-it’s just that I’m not that comfortable with little kids.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Well, that’s because you haven’t been around them much. This is good practice. I mean, you are gonna be a mom someday, right?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Mmm, yeah, sure.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Oh-ho-ho! I haven’t seen this trick in years. It’s called the dove pan. You let everyone see the pan is empty, but there’s a secret compartment in the lid. And then you open it and produce a live… Don’t look in there.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: The apartment.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Oh, a little Red Dead Redemption, huh?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Yes.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: How come you’re not doing a mission? You’re just wandering around.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Had a rough night. I thought I’d go for a walk and clear my head.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Some people go outside and do that.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: It’s after nine o’clock, at this hour the streets of Pasadena are teeming with drunken sailors and alley cats.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: You want to talk about it?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: No. I think I’ll just go in this saloon and drink my troubles away.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: You know digital alcohol is never a solution. What’s going on?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Hard as this may be to believe, it’s possible that I’m not boyfriend material.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Glad I was sitting down for that. Did you and Amy get in a fight?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Amy had a fight. I was being perfectly reasonable. I’m gonna have a whiskey. Do you want anything?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: No, I can’t. I’m playing Grand Theft Auto later. Look, I’m no expert in women.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I’ll say.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: That’s not necessary when someone’s trying to help you.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I’m sorry. It’s the alcohol talking. Go on.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Sometimes with women you want to listen to what upsets them and then show them that you can grow and change.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Nuts to that. What else you got?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I don’t know what to tell you. Buy her something.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: How does that work?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Well, you skip over any attempt to repair your emotional connection and you win back her affection with an empty financial gesture.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Well, that approach has Sheldon Cooper written all over it.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Glad I could help.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: It’s appreciated. And if you ever manage to find a woman again, I’ll be glad to return the favour.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: The birthday party.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: And now, all the rings are magically linked together. My fiancee’s wearing a magic ring, too. It made all my money disappear.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Oh, ah, right. (Bangs drum and cymbal) And now, the great Howdini’s next miraculous illusion.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: When are we gonna have cake?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: After you’ve been thoroughly amazed.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: But we want cake now.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Well, you’re not getting cake right now, capisce?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Okay. Okay. Now, my lovely assistant is going to bring me an ordinary pitcher of milk.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I know how you do that trick.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Do you know how to pipe down?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Okay, we’re going to roll up this newspaper.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: It’s a fake pitcher.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: You got wax in your ears? The man said it’s an ordinary pitcher. Howdini.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Okay, we’re going to stick this in here (puts newspaper into trouser waistband) and then I’m going to pour in the milk. I hope this works, because I didn’t bring a change of pants.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Look, I Googled it. It’s a fake pitcher.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: That’s it. No cake for you. Anyone else want to join the No Cake Club?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: She’s just kidding, boys and girls. Everyone gets cake.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Not him.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Just give me the pitcher. Behold! Wrong pitcher.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Bernadette’s car.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I told you I’m not good with kids.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Yes, you did. Oh, I think my crotch is starting to curdle.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: The thing is, my mother worked full-time. I had to take care of my brothers and sisters.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Yeah, so?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Ugh, it was horrible. With their snotty noses and their poopy diapers and their little shrieky voices, always complaining. I don’t want to get dressed. Joey keeps spitting in my mouth. This isn’t the way Mom makes waffles. Well, okay, put your hand in here. Let’s see how you like this waffle!

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: All right, settle down. Red light. Red light, red light! Okay, we’re fine.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I’m sorry. I know it makes me sound like a bad person, but I just don’t like children.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Yeah, no, we all got that. But don’t you think it’ll be different when the child is ours?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Right, when it’s our kid that’s ruined my body and kept me up all night and I’ve got no career and no future and nothing to be happy about for the next 20 years, sure, that’ll be completely different.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Well, yeah.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: A jewellery store.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I don’t think there’s anything in this jewellery store that Amy would appreciate more than the humidifier we were just looking at at Sears.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Oh, my God, now I know what I sound like to you when I say stupid stuff.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Ooh, a pocket watch.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Okay, I don’t think Amy wants a pocket watch.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: No, but maybe she wants a man with a pocket watch.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Still saying stupid stuff. Ooh, does she like bracelets?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Well, she’s very fond of her silver one that says allergic to penicillin. Maybe they have a dressier version of that?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Well, how are we doing this afternoon? Are we looking for anything special? Perhaps a ring for the lady?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: (Snorts) Trust me, we are not a couple.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Excuse me. I don’t see why you get to snort derisively and point that out. You’d be lucky to land a fella like me.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Fine, go ahead.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: (Snorts) Trust me, we are not a couple.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: My apologies. How can I help you today?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: He’s in trouble with his girlfriend and needs to buy her a present.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Great, trouble with girlfriends is what’s putting my daughter through USC.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Ooh, are these real diamonds?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Yes. Channel set baguettes, 20 points total weight.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Remarkable. Diamonds, crystallized carbon. Every day, people go to the grocery store and come home with sacks full of carbon in the form of charcoal briquettes that they toss in their barbeques and set on fire. But just because you’ve got some carbon with the atoms stacked neatly, you expect me to plunk down thousands of dollars.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Actually, that’s only 750. Everything’s on sale.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Really. Talk to me about that pocket watch.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: The apartment. The guys are playing Donkey Kong Jenga.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I’m still trying to wrap my mind around it. I always thought I’d be a dad someday.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Oh, me, too. You’re so caring. I’ve often pictured you guiding a young boy into manhood.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: There you go, Howard. Sounds like Raj’ll have your babies, problem solved.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Hey, just because a man shows caring for another man doesn’t mean he’s displaying the love that dare not speak its name. Did she definitely say she didn’t want kids?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Yeah, she doesn’t like them. And from what I saw, the feeling was mutual.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: What are you gonna do?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I don’t know. I can’t see a life where I don’t have kids. I mean, people have kids. I mean, even Donkey Kong had Donkey Kong Jr. So he could teach someone how to kidnap princesses and throw barrels at Italian plumbers.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: You know, there’s no guarantee even if you have kids that you’re going to like them.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Wow, that’s rough. Where’d you get that?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: It’s right off the dust jacket of my mom’s last book.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Maybe me and Bernadette aren’t right for each other.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Look, Howard, I’d say there’s a lot of fish in the sea, but I watched you dangle your hook in the water for years. Do not throw her back.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I don’t want to, but this is kind of a deal breaker.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: What’s your mom going to say if you call off the wedding?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Huh, it’ll kill her. On the other hand, if I don’t give her grandchildren, that’ll kill her, too. So, either way, on the Mom front, I’m golden.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Penny’s apartment.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: What time did you tell Amy to be here?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Eight o’clock. (Sheldon checks pocket watch) Sheldon, that pocket watch is ridiculous.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Nonsense. I look like a train conductor. Under what pretext did you lure her here?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I said, hey, want to come over and hang out?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Good, good, if you had said something clever, she might’ve gotten suspicious.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Hey.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Hi.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: What’s he doing here?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Okay, he wants to talk to you.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Well, I don’t want to talk to him. And I’m pretty disappointed in you, too. Although we both know that won’t last.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Sheldon, you’re up.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Thank you. Amy, I’d like to apologize. Your accomplishment was impressive. And I’m proud of you.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: We both know that’s your koala face.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I told you.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Okay, look, he bought you this.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Jewellery? Seriously? Sheldon, you are the most shallow, self-centred person I have ever met. Do you really think another transparently manip..oh! It’s a tiara! A tiara! I have a tiara! Put it on me, put it on me, put it on me, put it on me, put it on me, put it on me, put it on me.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: You look beautiful.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Of course I do, I’m a princess, and this is my tiara!

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: You’re right, the tiara was too much.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Howard’s bedroom.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Howard! Bernadette’s… Oh, she slipped right by me.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Here’s your vest back.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: You should keep it. You could wear it again sometime.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Where?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I don’t know, hunting?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Don’t forget to talk to her about this mishegas where I don’t get grandkids!

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Don’t worry, Ma. I will, as soon as I can figure out a way to bring up such a sensitive issue!

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I guess you talked to your mom, huh?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: I was upset. My mom can be a pretty good shoulder to cry on, if the smell of Bengay doesn’t burn your eyes.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Look, it’s obvious having kids is really important to you, and I think I came up with a solution.

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Really? That’s great. What?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Well, seeing as how I make way more money than you anyway, what if I work and you stay home with the kids?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Me?

episode_name: Series 05 Episode 12 – The Shiny Trinket Maneouvre
dialogue: Yeah. You know, you’ll watch Barney and pull Cheerios out of their noses and go on play dates, and I’ll work and have conversations with people my own age and enjoy my life.

dialogue: Yeah.

dialogue: Yay, so we’re good.

dialogue: Yeah, we’re good.

Precisely, I didn’t do anything. Now does someone feel like checking her emotional math?
Keep going, buddy, you’re doing great.
Sheldon, I’m your girlfriend, and you should have taken my side. That’s it. End of story. Good night.
Wow, Amy’s mad and Leonard was right. What a weird day.
The Cheesecake Factory.
Hey. Sorry this took so long. But you used to work here, you know how it is.
Kitchen slammed again?
No, I’m a terrible waitress, remember?
So, is there anything I can do to help you with the move tomorrow?
Now that you mention it, I was thinking tomorrow might not be great.
What’s your excuse this time?
No excuse. It’s just, you know, I’m Jewish, and technically, we’re not supposed to drive or carry anything on the Sabbath. So this one’s on God.
That might be a little more convincing if you didn’t have a mouthful of bacon cheeseburger.
My religion’s kinda loosey-goosey. Basically, as long as you got your schmekel clipped and don’t wear a cross, you’re good.
Howie, you promised you’d move.
And I will.
Yeah, right.
I will. I’m obviously not going to live in my mother’s house for the rest of my life. I’m not a child.
I’ve seen her burp you.
She did not burp me. She was patting me on the back, and I happened to burp. Don’t you have other tables you should be waiting on?
Yeah, but I told you, I’m not good at my job. Bernadette, listen to me. He is never gonna leave.
I’m starting to think you’re right.
All right, I’ve had enough of this. I’m a grown man, I have a successful career, for the love of God, I’ve been to space. I will move out when I’m ready, and I don’t need anyone badgering me into it.
Wow, excuse me.
That was just for her benefit. I’ll move tomorrow. I love you. Don’t leave me.
Amy’s apartment.
(Knock, knock, knock) Amy. (Knock, knock, knock) Amy. (Knock, knock, knock) Angry Amy.
What?
I’ve been thinking about what happened, and I hope this gift will make things better.
Star Trek DVDs? Why would I want this?

First of all, you’re welcome. And furthermore, not being familiar with Wil Wheaton’s body of work, there was no way for you to know you were being rude to a national treasure. Get ready for 130 hours of I told you so. (She hands him back the DVDs and slams the door) Fine. I’ll just tell you what happens. Episode one, Encounter at Farpoint. Fade in. The new Enterprise heads out on its maiden voyage to contact the Bandi people of Deneb IV. Enter Wesley Crusher, played by my buddy… (Amy opens door, grabs DVDs, slams door again) She’s hooked.
Howard’s bedroom.
Wow. An end of an era.
Boy, if these walls could talk.
They’d say, why does he touch himself so much?
Yeah. I can’t believe I’m not going to live here anymore. This has always been my bedroom. Right here is where my mom used to mark my height.
Oh, yeah. Fifth grade. Sixth grade. Seventh grade. Eighth grade. Ninth grade.

I remember when I was five, hiding under this desk with all my Halloween candy. Had some Peanut M&M’S, went into my first anaphylactic shock and had to be rushed to the hospital. Came home, celebrated with a Snickers, went into my second anaphylactic shock.
When did you figure out you were allergic to nuts?
Sometime around the third Almond Joy.
Okay. You want to start loading this stuff into the truck?
Yeah, I guess. Hey, would you do me a favour? Go on ahead. I just want one last moment alone in my old room.
We’re not standing outside by the U-Haul while you fondle yourself.
Fine, let’s go.
The Cheesecake Factory Bar.
Hey. What brings you in?
Penny, if you wouldn’t mind, I’d like to have a conversation about girls.
I had a feeling we’d have a talk like this sooner or later. Are you finally getting fuzz in weird places?
Penny, please, I’m on the horns of a relationship dilemma. And for the record, I had a full pubis of hair by the time I was 19.
And for the record, bleugh. So what are you drinking?
Well, it’s been a rough day. I usually go chamomile tea, but I don’t think that’s going to cut it.
You could have a Long Island Iced Tea.
Will that calm my nerves?
It’s calmed the pants off me a couple of times.
Sold.
Oh. So, the heart you got from the wizard giving you trouble?
The trouble isn’t with me, Penny, it’s with your gender. Someday, scientists will discover that second X chromosome contains nothing but nonsense and twaddle.
Yeah, Amy told me what happened. Look, just apologize. It’ll warm her twaddle.

It’s a Band-Aid at best. See, the core problem is that Amy and Wil do not like each other. Which is baffling because they’re both crazy about me. And I like them, which indicates they’re bright and interesting and/or were on Star Trek.
Honey, you can’t make people like each other.

Not true. Leonard made me like you. And let me tell you, that was a hard row to hoe. Cheers, pal. Ooh. Boy, that is a treat that’s hard to beat. Get the Mad Hatter on the horn, I’m having a tea party.
You might want to pace yourself.
I drink tea all the time. I think I know what I’m doing.
Far be it from me to criticize a man with a full pubis. Look, Sheldon, your problem is not Wil Wheaton, okay? Your problem is the way you treated Amy.
My problem is I’m out of tea.
Come on, someone insulted your girlfriend and you just let him do it. I thought you Texas guys stood up for your womenfolk.
Penny, please, I think I’ve evolved beyond my simple rustic upbringing.
Sorry.
On the other hand, that low-down polecat done wronged my woman.
Welcome to Long Island, Tex.
Amy deserves better. You know, when we buy the Planter’s deluxe mix, she eats all the Brazil nuts so I don’t have to look at them. She’s a unique blend of saint and squirrel.
Yeah, that she is. Here you go.
I’m a callous egomaniac. She’s gonna leave me.
No, she won’t.
No, she won’t. I’m great.
Howard and Bernadette’s apartment.
Okay, I have now officially moved out of my mother’s house. You are now the only woman in my life who I’ll see naked in the bathroom.
I know this wasn’t easy. You doing okay?
Oh, I’m fine. It’s just her I’m worried about.
Aw, she’ll be okay. She’s a grown woman.
I know. It’s just ever since my dad left, I’ve felt responsible for her.
That’s a lot for a kid to deal with.
She was just so sad all the time. I was the only person who could cheer her up. Well, me and Ben and Jerry.
She’s lucky you were there.

You know, she’s why I first got into magic. I would do little shows for her, hang up a bedsheet like it was a curtain, put on a top hat and cape. And part way through the act, I would say I needed a volunteer from the audience to be my beautiful assistant and invite her up on stage. I can still remember the way she’d smile. For a few minutes, she’d forget how lonely she was.
Aw, crap. Let’s go.
Where we going?
Grab a box. We’ll sleep at your mother’s place tonight.
No, but I want to live here.
Well, you should’ve thought of that before you told me the stupid magic trick story.
Can’t we talk about this?
No husband of mine is gonna break his mother’s heart!
Wil Wheaton’s house.
(Knock, knock, knock) Wil Wheaton! (Knock, knock, knock) Wil Wheaton! Wait, how many was that?
Hey, Sheldon, what’s up?
Wouldn’t you like to know?
Have you been drinking?
Just tea. S’the best tea I’ve ever had.
Why are you here?
I’ll tell you. I’m from Texas. Need I say more?
Yeah, actually, a little more would be helpful.
You insulted my woman. I’m here to defend her honour. Two! It was two. (Knock, knock, knock) Wil Wheaton! Now prepare yourself for what may come.
Oh, Sheldon, do you really think we’re gonna fight?
My fists are not up here because I’m milking a giant invisible cow. They’re up to beat an apology out of you.
Okay, I’m sorry.
Well, that was a long bus ride for not very much.
Are you okay?

You’re asking a lot of questions, Wil Wheaton. As a matter of idle curiosity, which of your shrubberies do you feel would benefit from a thorough vomiting? Never mind, I’ll choose. (Vomits) You were so good in Stand by Me.
The apartment.

Hello, I’m Dr. Sheldon Cooper. Welcome to Sheldon Cooper Presents Fun with Flags. Get ready for a very special episode where we explore the flags of the popular entertainment franchise, Star Trek. And to help us, I’m pleased to introduce a special guest, surprisingly, it only took gas money and the promise of free food to get him here, Mr. LeVar Burton.
Hey, Sheldon, it’s a pleasure to be here. Well, we’ve got some interesting flags for…
Cut. Yikes, this guy is worse than Wil Wheaton.
I don’t know what she’s talking about, but I’m obligated to agree with her. She’s my girlfriend.
Ah, I hear you, brother. I still get lunch, right?
The cafeteria. Sheldon is drawing on a napkin.
What are you drawing over there?
It’s a hypothetical containment field for a Frisbee-sized wormhole that could serve as a portal to a parallel universe.
Oh, you silly doodlebug.
You know, a lot of scientists believe that making contact with other life-forms would probably not end well for us.
It’s a Frisbee-sized wormhole, Leonard. You can block it with a Frisbee. Calm down. (Hands Howard the napkin)
Do you expect me to build this?
I expect you to wipe the pudding off your chin. Gentlemen.
Have you guys ever noticed that Sheldon always disappears every day at two forty-five?
Really?
He probably just goes to the bathroom.
Actually, no, he goes to the bathroom at eight a.m. with optional follow-ups at one forty-five and seven ten high-fibre Fridays.
It’s sad that you know that.
Oh, that’s just the tip of the sadness iceberg.

I’m looking at his public calendar. Two forty-five to three-oh-five, nothing. Yesterday, two forty-five to three-oh-five, nothing, last week, nothing, last month, nothing. He never has anything booked during that time.
Twenty minutes a day, completely unaccounted for.
We should figure out where he goes.
Ooh, this is exciting. Like one of my classic murder mystery dinner parties.
Right, the case of who murdered three Saturday nights of my life?
Colonel Koothrapali in the kitchen with the olive spread.
It was tapenade and you guys suck.
Penny’s apartment. Penny is texting.
So, how was work today?
Well, I spent most of the afternoon growing isotopically pure crystals for neutrino detection.
That sounds like fun.
Yeah, it was.
Oh, good, I guessed right.
Who you talking to?
Oh, just this guy I met at school.
Oh, great. We’re still dating, right?
Relax. He’s just a friend. We’re doing an oral report together. He’s really nice.
I’m sorry, what was that? I had a little stroke after oral.
Would you stop? Look, he just moved here from London, okay? He doesn’t really know anybody.
Oh, good, an English accent, the sexiest accent you can have.
No. That’s not true. There’s French, there’s Italian. No, you’re right, it’s the best.
Did you tell him you have a boyfriend?
It didn’t come up.
Well, maybe you should tell him.
What am I supposed to say?
Say, can’t talk right now, hanging with my boyfriend. England sucks, you suck, USA number one.
Fine. Hanging with my boyfriend. Talk to you later. Happy?
Yes. Thank you.
Mm-hmm. Hmm.
What did he say?
Nothing.
What?
Did your boyfriend make you type that?
I hate this guy.
Don’t be like that.
Come on, trust me, he’s hitting on you.
No, he’s not. We’re just friends. Look, is this gonna be a problem? Because he’s supposed to come over tomorrow to work.
Really? Here?
If it makes you uncomfortable, I’ll switch partners, even though the thing’s due next week and everyone already has a partner and I’ll probably end up failing the class.
That’d be great. Thank you.
The corridor outside Sheldon’s office.
Two forty-four, Right on schedule. Hey, Sheldon.
Oh, hello.
Raj and I are heading over to the genetics lab to pet the glow-in-the-dark bunny. Want to come with us?
No, thank you.
Are you sure? They turn off the lights, and it’s like a cute little laser show that poops all over the place.
I’m quite sure. Good day.
Well, where are you going?
Where are you going?
We just told you.
I just told you.
No, you didn’t.
Well, it’s your word against mine; see you in court.
Should we follow him?
I don’t know, I’m torn. I want to know where he’s going, but now I kind of want to play with the bunny.
Hi, guys.
Hey, Alex, do you know where your boss just went?
No.
Don’t you know his schedule?
All I know is corduroy makes too much noise and I have to go find quieter pants.
Come on.
Boy, what I wouldn’t give to get her out of those pants and into something a little more stylish.
A corridor in the basement. Sheldon takes out a key, unlocks a door and enters.
This is where he goes? What’s in there?
I think it’s an old storage room.
What could he be doing in there every day for twenty minutes?
Well, he’s not doing twenty-minute abs, because if he were, he would have way better abs. Can you hear anything?
Not yet. What are you doing?
I’m listening.
Can’t you face the other way and listen?
I can’t do anything right for you, can I?
What the hell is he up to?
He is kind of a weirdo. Maybe he’s got Leonard Nimoy chained up in there. Or Bill Gates. Or Stephen Hawking.
Why would he chain up Stephen Hawking?
Howard, please, you can’t treat the man differently just because he’s disabled. That’s not okay.
The apartment.
If you’re wondering why I’ve been staring through the peephole, I’m trying to get a look at this guy who’s coming over to Penny’s.
To be honest, I didn’t know you were here.
It’s not a big deal. He’s just in her history class. They’re working on a project together. I don’t even know why I care. You know what, I don’t care.
You think you don’t care?
This is silly. I have nothing to worry about.
Oh, I don’t know. I mean, statistically speaking, I’m sure you have something to worry about.
What do you mean?

Well, if we assume your looks are average, yeah, right off the bat, fifty percent of men on Earth are more attractive than you. That’s one point five billion handsome lads standing by, waiting to rain on your parade.
Well, yeah, but this isn’t just about looks. I’m, I’m way above average in a lot of other things.
Not height, vision, athleticism, or ability to digest dairy products.
I’m talking about important things like emotional maturity.
You were just spying on your girlfriend through a peephole.
I liked it better when you thought I wasn’t here.

I’m not saying you don’t have attractive qualities. Your choice of friends is impeccable, you’re a good sleeper, and last but not least, you buy the grapes I like. You’re a real catch compared to some snoring guy with a fridge full of lousy grapes.
None of this matters. I trust that Penny cares about me, and nothing’s gonna happen with this guy.
Well, unless of course he’s a skilled hypnotist.
What?
While unlikely, it’s still a statistical possibility. She might be performing sexual acts with him and not even know it.
Now you’re just being ridiculous.
Am I? The mind’s a mysterious thing, Leonard. He could be having the time of his life while she thinks she’s a chicken pecking for corn.
The university basement.
Look at us, sneaking around in the middle of the night like a couple of cat burglars.
I think we’re more like ninjas.
I don’t want to be a ninja, I want to be a cat burglar.
Fine, I’ll be a ninja, you be a cat burglar.
No, we both have to be the same thing. Okay, we’re ninjas.
Thank you.
But next time, we’ll be cat burglars.
It’s locked.
Are you sure?
Yes, I’m sure. Now, you stand guard, I’m going to…
It’s locked.
Just keep an eye out. I’ll have this open in a minute.
When did you learn how to pick locks?
When I was starting to do magic in junior high, I thought I could be an escape artist like Harry Houdini.
How did that work out?
Pretty good. I managed to escape friends, popularity, and every party thrown in a twelve mile radius. There. Ready?
Hold on, hold on.
What?
Sheldon is a very smart man, and he obviously wants to keep this a secret.
Yeah, so?
What if it’s booby-trapped?
Don’t worry, I’m one step ahead of him.
Great, what’s your pl… (Howard pushes him inside)
Are we good?
Yeah. Huh. Forty-three? What the hell does that mean?
I don’t know. The solution to an equation?
Maybe. It’s a prime number. Encryption systems are built on prime numbers.
What kind of secret does Sheldon have to encrypt?
He’s always been very cagey about what he puts in his egg salad to make it so tasty.
It’s paprika.
Really? Well, oh, okay, one mystery solved.
The apartment.
Okay, good night.
Thanks, Cole. See you at school.
See you.
I’ll be right back.
I thought you left a long time ago.
‘sup?
Hey.
You, uh, moving into the apartment on the fifth floor?
No, I was just visiting a friend.
Oh, cool. That cute blonde on four?
Yeah. You know her?
I, well, I see her around. I like to keep my distance because her boyfriend is a pretty scary dude.
Really?
Yeah. He’s ganged up.
She told me he’s a scientist.
That’s the name of his gang. The Scientists. They are crazy.
Well, thanks for the tip.
No problem, brother. Stay frosty. (Cole leaves. Leonard spots Penny watching.) We’re still dating, right?
The cafeteria.
Oh, hello, Dr. Hofstadter.
Hey, Alex, and call me Leonard. Dr. Hofstadter is my father. And my mother. And my sister. And our cat. Although, I’m pretty sure Dr. Boots Hofstadter’s degree was honorary.
May I join you, Leonard?
Sure.
Thanks.
Hey, Alex, let me ask you something. My girlfriend knows this guy at school. He’s got an English accent.
Ooh, I love English accents.
Yeah, you all do. Anyway, I feel like he’s hitting on her. She says he’s just being nice and that I should trust her.
It’s probably harmless. You know how it is. I’m sure you get hit on all the time.
Right. Because girls are always like, ooh, that guy owns two Star Trek uniforms and gets a lot of ear infections. I got to get me some of that.
I don’t know, I bet it happens more than you realize.
Trust me, it doesn’t.
You sure? You’re cute, you’re funny. Maybe you’re getting hit on, and you don’t even know it.
Really?
Yep, pretty sure.
Okay, I got to get back to work. Thanks for listening.
No problem.
Hope-hope no girls rip my clothes off on the way.
Raj’s office.
Come on, we’re smart guys. We can figure this out.
Forty-three. What is forty-three? Besides my mom’s neck size.
It’s the atomic number for technetium.
That stuff’s radioactive.
Do you think he’s building a bomb?
Ah, it took him two years to put together that Lego Death Star, I’m not worried.
Ooh, this could be something. forty-three is the number of calories in half a cup of fat-free yoghurt.
Why would you know that?
I’m sorry. We can’t all eat whatever we want and still stay thin. Wait, in the Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy, isn’t forty-three the answer to the question of life, the universe,and everything?
That’s forty-two, dumb-ass.
Hey, hey. Feelings.
We should stop. I’m exhausted.
Yeah, me, too. We’ve got more important things to do. Who cares what stupid forty-three means?
Not me.
Let’s go home. You want to get something to eat?
Sounds good.
What the balls is forty-three?
I have to know!
The stairwell.
Hi.
Hey, shouldn’t you be out with your gang, spray painting equations on the side of buildings?
Come on, I’m sorry.
I just can’t believe you don’t trust me.
I do, of course I do.
Then why did you embarrass me in front of my friend, who, by the way, knew exactly who you were?
Really?
Your picture’s on my refrigerator.
Oh. You know, I’m really starting to not like this guy.
What is your problem? Do you use up all your thinking at work and then have none left over for when you get home?

I don’t know. It-it-it’s hard sometimes. Everywhere you go, guys hit on you, even if I’m standing right there. And they’re all taller than me. Why is everyone taller than me? You know what, this is all in my head. It’s my problem, not yours.
Leonard, why do you always do this? Listen to me, you’re the one I’m with. You know I love you, so will you please relax because you’re driving me crazy.
You know that’s the first time you ever said that you love me.
Yeah.
We’re just supposed to pretend it’s not a big deal?
That’s exactly what we’re gonna do because you’re about to make me cry, and we both know if I start crying, you’re gonna start crying.
You’re right, you should go.
All right.
She loves me. (Receives text) Hey, it’s Alex. Nice having coffee with you. If you want to talk more, I’m always available. Smiley face, smiley face. What a friendly girl.
The cafeteria.
Okay, picture’s up. Looks like the camera’s working.
That’s good quality video.
It better be. It’s the spare camera for the Mars rover.
How did you get your hands on that?
Million dollar camera, ten dollar lock.
Oh, my God, here he comes. This is it.
What the hell is that thing?
I don’t know.
This is Dr. Sheldon Cooper. Experimental log. Wormhole generator test forty-four.
Wormhole generator test? (On screen a wormhole appears)
The first forty-three parallel universes I’ve checked proved to be empty. I see no reason to suspect universe number forty-four will be any different. (Puts his head in the wormhole)
Oh, my God!
Holy crap!
Oh! It’s eating my face!
Aah! It’s eating his face!
I found your webcam and replaced the video feed. You two should be ashamed of yourselves.
Sheldon, we’re really sorry.
Yeah, really sorry.

Sorry? You may not realize it, but I have difficulty navigating certain aspects of daily life. You know, understanding sarcasm, feigning interest in others, not talking about trains as much as I want to. It’s exhausting. Which is why, for twenty minutes a day, I like to go down to that room, turn my mind off and do what I need to do to recharge.
But what are you doing in there?
And what does forty-three mean?
You don’t need to know, you don’t deserve to know, and you will never know.
Yeah, well, I know how to make your egg salad now.
The room in the basement. Sheldon enters, takes out a box, takes a beanbag from the box, then starts playing keepie-uppie,
One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight… Drat. I’m never going to get to forty-three again. One, two, three, four… Rats.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation
dialogue: Thanks. Guess who picked up his new car this morning?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation
dialogue: Yep. For as long as I can keep my mother out of it. If you want to check it out later, it’s parked right out front, space 294.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation
dialogue: Sheldon, someday, if you get a car, I’m sure they’ll give you another parking space.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation
dialogue: I don’t want another parking space. I want my parking space. It’s perfect. It’s a corner spot, cutting the risk of door-dings in half. It’s a mere 28 steps from the building entrance. The nearby tree provides shade on hot days and is also home to a delightful squirrel. Which is fortuitous because most squirrels are real jerks.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation
dialogue: Fun story. Meanwhile, you still don’t have a car.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation

dialogue: Are you listening to yourself?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation
dialogue: I always listen to myself. It’s one of the great joys of my life. Now, get your car out of my spot.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation
dialogue: Nope.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 09 – The Parking Spot Escalation
dialogue: Very well. You leave me no choice.

Oh, you poor thing. Is having a real-life girlfriend who has sex with you getting in the way of your board games?
Little bit, yeah.
The apartment.
Oh, great! I’ve always wanted to play Dungeons and Dragons.
Yeah, oh, I’m sorry. I should’ve mentioned this earlier. You’re not invited.
Why not?
Amy, from time to time, we men need to break free from the shackles of civility and get in touch with our primal animalistic selves.
By rolling dice and playing make-believe with little figurines?
Yeah, like a bunch of savages.
Howard and Bernadette’s apartment. Bernadette is on the webcam.
Saturday night? But I’ve been working late all week. That was gonna be our night.

But I have to go. We play as a group. If-if I’m not there, then everyone will blame you. They’ll be all, Bernadette ruined everything. She’s the worst. So, you see? I have to play Dungeons and Dragons for the marriage.
You’re an idiot.
I’m your idiot. Forever.
Raj’s apartment.
So, listen, I know we talked about getting a bite to eat in Silver Lake, and then seeing the Christmas lights in Griffith Park, but Leonard’s talking about a big D and D game at his place.
Saturday night just went from crazy to epic. Woo-hoo!
The apartment.
All right, Sheldon, to start our quest you need to open this little Christmas gift I got you.
A Christmas gift? You know I don’t enjoy Christmas.
What’s wrong with Christmas?
Oh, where to begin? Trees indoors. Overuse of the words ’tis and ’twas. And the absurd custom of one stocking. Everyone knows socks belong in pairs. Who uses one sock?
Pirate with a peg leg?
Actually that helps, thank you.
Would you just look inside?

Oh, a scroll. I like scrolls. They’re my third favourite system of transmitting the written word. After stone tablets and skywriting. You have all been summoned to join a thrilling Dungeons and Dragons adventure. Your quest begins in a secret northern village of elves who have all been massacred. I like where this is heading. Your task is to rescue their leader from a dungeon of ogres. Oh, that’s a saucy twist. That leader’s name, Santa Claus. No, no, no.
It’s actually ho, ho, ho, but you’ll get the hang of it. Thought it’d be fun to make a quest with a holiday theme.
Fun? Mixing Dungeons and Dragons with Christmas is like making a sandwich of grape jelly, the best-tasting jelly, and petroleum jelly, the worst-tasting jelly.
Okay, here we go. You find yourselves in the smoking remains of Santa’s village. Clearly, a great battle has taken place.
Oh, man, the first monster I see, I’m gonna sneak up behind him, whip out my wand, and shoot my magic all over his ass.
Do you hear yourself when you say these things?
Okay, there are ogre tracks and a trail of broken candy canes in the snow. Sheldon, what do you do?
I signal my contempt for your cruel plan to shove Christmas joy down my throat by making a gesture that says get a load of this guy.
Fine. Howard, what do you do?
I follow the ogre tracks, checking for secret doors along the way.
And you discover a secret door leading to a dark corridor.
Okay, guys, let’s make a plan, spell casters in the back, warriors in the front.
No, screw that noise, I’m going in. Hang on, Santa, I’m coming for you.
Okay, you run into a room full of weapons, hit a trip wire, a cannon blows your face off, you die, you’re out of the game.
But, a cannon? Am I really out of the game?
Lucky.
Okay, come on, moving on.
Wait, doesn’t anyone have a rod of resurrection? Because if you’ve got one, I need it bad. Get in here with your rod and give it to me.
Okay, you need to say these things in your head before you say them out loud.

Hey, guys. I don’t mean to interrupt your little game, but I thought you’d like to see what you’re missing out on. So, Bernadette? Bernadette’s wearing leopard-print pumps and a rack-tastic red dress from Forever 21. And there’s Amy, showing all kinds of ankle. In an outfit I’m assuming is from Forever 63. And I, myself am wearing a little number that got me out of two speeding tickets and jury duty.
I know they’re making a rhetorical point, I just don’t know what it is.
See you, boys. We are going drinking.
Uh, wait, can I come with you? My character died.
Sorry, Raj, it’s girls’ night out.
Maybe another time.
Okay…
Come on.
Ooh! Girls’ night, girls’ night! Ooh! Ooh!
How does he not hear that?
A bar.
So, what’s the plan? Are we gonna teach our fellas a lesson by getting stinking drunk, luring strange men into the bathroom, and turning the toilet stall into a temple of the senses?
No!
No!
Geez, who’s Forever 63 now?
Can we get another bottle of champagne for the table? Don’t worry. It’s my treat.
Thanks.
Wow, you should come to girls’ night more often. And not just because if you weren’t here, this would be a can of Pabst.
My pleasure, nothing makes me happier than the chance to spoil a lady. Just ask my dog. My vet says if I give her any more foie gras, she’s going to die of gout.
Hey, let’s help Raj meet a girl tonight.
No, no, no, I’m fine.
Okay, wait, are we talking one-night stand or do we want to get him into a relationship?
Let’s get him laid!
Stop it. You’re ruining girls’ night.
Raj, you’re a great guy, you’re in a bar full of single women, let us help you.
Yeah, you’re a real catch. I know you’re shy, but that doesn’t mean you shouldn’t have someone wonderful in your life.
That’s sweet of you. But what can you do to help?
We’ll nose around, see if we can find a nice girl, and then introduce you.
Okay. Well, a couple of things. Don’t tell them I come from money. I want them to love me for me. They must be insanely hot. Like, nines or tens.
Nines or tens?
Okay, an eight is acceptable if she’s willing to bring another eight to the hot tub.
Bottom line, you’ll take any woman who’ll have you, right?
In a New Delhi minute.
The apartment.
I don’t remember you buying these miniatures in my store.
Oh, uh, yeah. I got ’em on Amazon.
Sure. I get it. Why support a friend when you can support a multinational conglomerate that is crushing the life out of that friend?
I know, but when I shop online, I can do it on the toilet.
Have you seen my store? The whole place is a toilet.
Can we please move this along?
Yeah, sorry. Uh, you come to the end of the tunnel and find a large chest. What do you do? And, Howard, do not say, I feel up the large chest.
Excuse me, I’m a married man now. I wasn’t going to say anything so juvenile.
Great. What do you do?
I walk up to the large chest, bury my face in it and go “blublublublublublublublu”
I open the chest.
It’s locked, but suddenly the door behind you slams shut and now the walls of the room start closing in.
That’s not good. My character and I both have claustrophobia.
Glowing letters appear on the chest that read, If squashed to death you wish not to be, sing of Svaty Vaclav and his victory.
Who the hell is Svaty Vaclav?
Walls are getting closer.
Oh, boy, happy place, happy place.
Wait, Svaty Vaclav was the Duke of Bohemia.
You’re ten seconds away from getting crushed. Nine, eight.
What are we supposed to do?
Seven, six.
Wait, wait. Svaty Vaclav is better known as Good King Wenceslas from the beloved Victorian Christmas carol.
Never heard of it. Must be the one Christmas song not written by a Jewish guy.
Three, two.
Somebody sing the damn song.
Good King Wenceslas looked out, on the feast of Stephen. When the snow lay ’round about, deep and crisp and even
The walls are getting slower.
Brightly shone the moon that night, though the frost was cruel. When a poor man came in sight gathering winter fuel.
The walls stop. You’re safe.
That was amazing, Sheldon.
How did you know that?

It was simple. I combined a well-known historical fact about Bohemia with the memory of my grandparents, Mee-Maw and Pop-Pop, singing Christmas carols while I sat in front of the fire and tried to build a high-energy particle accelerator out of Legos.
Okay, continuing our quest.

W-W-Wait. There’s still four more verses. You don’t sing a song and not finish it. Hither, page, and stand by me, if thou know’st it, telling. Yonder peasant, who is he? Where and what his dwelling? Brightly shone the moon that night, though the frost…
The bar.
Looks like he’s doing pretty good.
Of course he is. Look, that girl just got dumped by her boyfriend. She’s angry, she’s drunk, and her favorite movie is Slumdog Millionaire. I mean.
That is some low-hanging fruit.
Oh, here he comes.
So, how’d it go?
Great. I bought her a couple of drinks, and she gave me her e-mail address.
Ooh!
Jennifer at not-even-if-you-were-the-last-guy-on-earth dot loser.
What?
I’m sorry, Raj.
Why can’t I find someone? I’m smart, I’ve got a cool job, and my naturally bronzed complexion means I can pull off mustard yellow in a way most guys can’t.
Oh, honey, it’s not you, it’s them.
No, it’s not. She was too beautiful for me.
Why would you say that?
It’s true. I’m always attracted to women I can’t have. I do it all the time. I did the same thing with the two of you.
The two of them? I don’t understand.
Well, uh, there was a time when I had a thing for Penny, and I thought she was into me, too, because she got drunk and naked and climbed into bed with me. But apparently I misread those signals.
And you liked Bernadette also?
That was before Penny. I make it a rule to only fall for one of my friends’ girlfriends at a time. I’m very old-fashioned that way.
So at, uh, some point, you probably had a thing for me, too.
No, not really.
Oh, come on, Raj, not even a little bit?
Not that I can think of.
Think harder.
Nope. I guess the heart wants what the heart wants. Or in this case, doesn’t, I mean, at all. What?
The apartment. Sheldon is still singing.
Ye who now will bless the poor, shall yourselves find blessing. Ba-da-bum.
Done?
I think the word you’re looking for is bravo.
Okay, you leave the room and find yourself standing before a pool of melted snowmen.
Melted snowmen? Are there carrots and lumps of coal in the water?
I don’t know. What’s the difference?
Well it’s a game of the imagination, Leonard. Paint a picture.
Fine. You leave the room and find yourself standing before a pool of melted snowmen. There are carrots and lumps of coal in the water.
What happened to the top hats and the corncob pipes?
You see those, too.
Oh, it’s like I’m really there.
I gotta tell you, this, this is the most holiday fun I’ve had since my therapist changed my anxiety medication and I stopped caring about the blood in my stool.
Good story.
What are you drinking there? A little eggnog?
Yes. What, is there a problem?
No, it’s nice to see you enjoying a holiday beverage. Pretty Christmassy.
Since when is eggnog a Christmas drink? Eggs are available all year ’round. I’ve been known to enjoy this poolside.
Come on, Sheldon. You know all the Christmas stories, and the carols, you’ve got an eggnog moustache going on there. Just admit it. You’re getting a little Yuletide spirit.
Oh, don’t be silly. Christmas is a bunch of baloney created by the tinsel industry. Why is this so important to you?
Honestly, because I had enough crappy Christmases as a kid and I’m tired of you sucking the joy out of them now.
What was so bad about them?

I grew up in a house full of crazy academics. Instead of leaving Santa milk and cookies, we had to leave him a research paper. And in the morning, you could tell he’d been there because the paper would be graded.
No wonder you love Christmas. That sounds amazing.
It wasn’t amazing. I got a C-minus four years in a row.
Yeah, I’m familiar with your work. C-minus was your gift.
The bar.
Amy, I’m really sorry. I didn’t mean to upset you.
It’s fine. I’m used to being the girl who never gets looked at twice. I didn’t have my first kiss till I was 22, and the guy only did it so I’d give him back his insulin.
Sometimes the pancreas wants what the pancreas wants.
Forget it. I don’t expect you guys to understand.
I understand. In seventh grade, I played Spin the Bottle and it landed on Alina Shankar. She said if I came near her, she would break the bottle and cut me.
You think that’s bad? In college, I passed out at a frat party and woke up with more clothes on.
Sometimes I get so lonely, I sit on my left hand until it goes numb, then I put it in my right hand and pretend I’m holding hands with another person.
I do that, too. Sometimes the left hand tries to cop a feel. And I let it.
It’s kind of nice to talk to someone who understands what it feels like to be alone.
It is, isn’t it?
But you’re not alone anymore. Now you’ve got Sheldon.
I do. And don’t worry, someday you’ll have somebody, too.
Thank you. I hope she’s half as lovely and amazing as you are.
Thank you, Rajesh. He wants me, I’m good. We can go now.
Damn it.
What?
Now that I know she doesn’t like me, I’m kind of into her.
The apartment. Sheldon is writing numbers on a whiteboard.
All right. I think I cracked the code to lower the drawbridge.
Great. Let’s do it. (They pick up bells and play according to the numbers. The tune is Jingle Bells)
The drawbridge is lowering.
My carpal tunnel’s acting up.
Play through the pain.

You did it. The drawbridge is down. You cross the chasm and find yourself in a small dungeon room. And in the corner, chained to the wall, you see a bloodied and beaten Santa Claus. He says, ho, ho, help me.
Yes, we found Santa. Christmas is saved. Don’t ever tell my mother I said that.
I take out my skeleton key and run to Santa to unchain him.
But first, I cast a spell of paralysis on Stuart and Howard.
Wait, what are you doing?

You can’t talk, you’re paralyzed. I get right up in Santa’s big, fat face and say, well, well, well, jolly old Saint Nick, we meet again. Yeah, I believe the last time we spoke was in the Baybrook Mall in Galveston, Texas, when I was five years old, isn’t that right?
Uh, okay.

My mother dragged me there and she plopped me down on your lap and you asked me what I wanted for Christmas. And I told you, my Pop-Pop, because that was the year my grandfather died. I missed him and I wanted him back.
This is weird, right?

Pop-Pop was the only one in my family who encouraged me to pursue science. But you didn’t bring him back, did you? No, instead, I got Lincoln Logs. Well, you can build a lot of neat things out of Lincoln Logs, but Pop-Pop ain’t one of ’em. And now you’re here asking me for something, to save you. Well, sorry, Mr. Kringle, but today’s not your day. I’m leaving you here to rot, and I hope the ogres feast on your bones. I take the skeleton key, and I toss it into the chasm, and on the way out, I give Santa a swift kick in his bowl full of jelly!
Okay. So Wolowitz and Stuart are paralyzed, Santa’s dead, and I picked this over having sex with my girlfriend.
The apartment, late at night.
Santa?
Oh, hello, Sheldon. You should be asleep.
Well, then, you shouldn’t have jingle bells on your boots.
Oh. I’ve been wanting to talk to you. I’m sorry I disappointed you when you were a little boy. I can do a lot of magical things, but unfortunately bringing your Pop-Pop back isn’t one of them.
I understand.
But I do have something special for you. Close your eyes.
Oh, I hope it’s a train.
Oh, it’s better than a train.
Two trains?
Better.
I’m getting three trains.
Okay, open ’em. (It’s a cannon, pointed at Sheldon) This is for leaving me in the dungeon to be eaten alive by ogres!
Wait, uh, uh, hang on. In my defense…
Ho, ho, ho, ya big dork. (Fires cannon)

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: The apartment.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Well, I must say, Leonard, when I first heard your idea for Giant Jenga, I was sceptical.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: I can’t blame you. Tiny Twister was a complete bust.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: No, I was wrong. The looming threat of being crushed under a pile of lumber does add a certain spice. I’ve never felt so alive. (Answers door) Oh, hello, Alex. Uh, let me go get you last night’s recordings.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: What recordings?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Well, you remember when you told me I talk in my sleep? Well, it occurred to me that, like most things I say, it’s probably pure gold. So I started recording it all, and now Alex gets to comb through eight hours of what I like to call Sheldon After Dark.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Hey, Leonard.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Hey. Just playing a little Giant Jenga here.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Oh, I know, I’m the one who had to buy him the helmet. So, do you have any plans this weekend?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Well, most of Saturday’s gonna be figuring out where to put this game when we’re done. How about you?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Oh, I’m gonna go see Kip Thorne give a lecture on subatomic space-time.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Ooh. That’s his take on John Wheeler’s quantum foam. That should be great.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Well, if you want, you can come with me.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Ah, I’d love to, but I’m supposed to hang out with Penny.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Well, bring her.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Well, she’s not really into that kind of stuff.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Yeah, okay. Well, if you want to hear about the lecture, I can tell you all about it at work, or, you know, over dinner sometime.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: What?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Jenga, I win!

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: The cafeteria.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Oh, come on, that can’t be true.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: I did the research. Tony the Tiger, Dig’em the Frog, Cap’n Crunch, Toucan Sam, Count Chocula, Trix the Rabbit, Snap, Crackle and Pop. Not one cereal mascot is a girl. It’s a total breakfast sausage fest.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Are we done with this?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Almost. Franken Berry, Boo Berry, Sugar Bear and the Honey Nut Cheerio bee, I believe his name is Buzz.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Terrific. Something weird happened and I don’t know what to do about it.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: What’s going on?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Sheldon’s assistant asked me on a date last night.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: How could you do that to me? You know I’ve been working it with Alex for weeks.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Working it? You can’t even talk to her.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: I talk with my eyes.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: You look like my little cousin when he’s dropping one in his diaper.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: She knows I have a girlfriend. It’s so weird.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Oh, my God. You’re loving this.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: To my bones. I mean, I’m not gonna do anything about it. I love Penny. It’s just nice to have a young, attractive woman sniffing around the goods.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: I both hate you and want to be you. This is Ryan Gosling all over again.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Ah, gentlemen, what is on the conversational menu this morning?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Leonard stole my woman, and he knew full well I was only six to eight months away from making my move.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: I didn’t steal anyone.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Your assistant is totally hitting on this jerk and he loves it.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Well, that’s not acceptable. I mean, I’m her boss. She needs to be solely focused on my needs, not distracted by your pasty, androgynous brand of sexuality.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: I’m androgynous?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Oh, please. Look at you with your pouty bee-stung lips.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: What do you guys think I should do?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: I say you tell Alex your heart belongs to Penny, I provide her a shoulder to cry on, and then roughly half a year later I give it to her good.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Amy’s apartment.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: I want to thank you all for coming on such short notice. Uh, in the past, I’ve reached out to each of you individually, but I believe my present situation requires the collective wisdom of the group, which as you can see from your commemorative T-shirts I have dubbed Sheldon Cooper’s Council of Ladies.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: What is happening?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: I need your advice about a delicate workplace situation. Uh, to protect those involved, I’ll be changing their names.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Who’s involved?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Well, a short, bespectacled colleague of mine who lives in the shadow of his brilliant roommate. Let’s call this colleague Ricardo Shilly-Shally.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: You’re talking about Leonard.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: No, no, Shilly-Shally has red hair and, uh, he briefly served in the Mexican Navy. Anyway, despite the fact that he has a girlfriend, Shilly-Shally has been the recipient of inappropriate workplace flirtations from a young lady.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: It’s your assistant Alex, isn’t it?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: No. No. No. This is Tondelaya della Ventimiglia.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Wait, what the hell’s going on with Leonard and Alex?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: No, uh, no, I’m sorry. Who’s talking about Leonard and Alex?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Fine. Ricardo and Tondelaya.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Okay, look, it’s not really about Ricardo and Tondelaya. It is really about her boss, who doesn’t quite know how to handle this situation and could use your advice, which is surprising because Dr. Einstein Von Brainstorm, he’s usually pretty smart about these things.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: I’m gonna kill her.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: I’m sure you’ve got nothing to worry about. Leonard would never cheat on you.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: She’s right. But say the word, I got a lab full of cocaine-addicted monkeys with nothing to lose. One of them could end up in the backseat of her car. Or her shower.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Ladies, ladies, please. We’re not here to talk about Penny, okay? We’re here to talk about me. Uh, I mean Einstein Von Brainstorm. Oh, darn it! All right, I guess the cat’s out of the bag. Let me explain what’s going on. Ricardo is really Leonard.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: We know what’s going on, Sheldon!

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Well, what should I do?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Well, Alex is your employee. If she’s doing something that’s making Leonard uncomfortable, you should talk to her.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Oh, no, he’s not uncomfortable at all. No, he’s loving it. Yeah, he’s strutting around like he’s five-foot-six.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: What? He’s loving it?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Sheldon, you need to talk to Alex right away.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Talk to her? That’s all you’ve got? With a cool name like Sheldon Cooper’s Council of Ladies, I really expected more. Give me back the T-shirts.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Sheldon’s office.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Alex, check my schedule. What does my afternoon look like?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: I think it’s pretty wide open. Oh, wait. Here’s something at four o’clock. Give Alex a talking to?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Well, that snuck up on us, didn’t it?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Is there a problem?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Let’s not call it a problem. Let’s call it an opportunity. To solve a serious problem.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: What did I do?

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: You don’t know? Oh, you poor dear. Your ovaries are squirting so much goofy juice into your brains you don’t even know which way is up. You made an inappropriate sexual advance towards Dr. Hofstadter.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: What? I didn’t make a sexual advance on anybody.

episode_name: Series 06 Episode 12 – The Egg Salad Equivalency
dialogue: Now, there’s no need to get defensive. I’m not unsympathetic to your plight. My father used to say that a woman is like an egg salad sandwich on a warm Texas day.
