episode_name: Series 06 Episode 16 – The Tangible Affection Proof
dialogue: Hello? Another medical emergency? What’s wrong with him now? I seriously doubt he was bitten by a Chinese bird spider. How exactly does a bump feel Asian? Just put him on the phone. Sheldon, I am not driving over there again. Because I drove over there yesterday for a brain tumour that turned out to be an ice cream headache. Yes, I still want to be your emergency contact. Yes, you can eat your ice cream too fast and also have a brain tumour. I’m on my way. Brain tumour would explain a lot.
(After a “previously on” sequence) A coffee shop

So then I went to Cambridge, which was wonderful not only because it’s a good school but because it totally looks like Hogwarts. That’s where I fell in love with astronomy, and now I’m an astrophysicist at Caltech, so I guess you could say, uh, Raj is my name and stars are my game. And rhyming is also my game. So, uh, two games. Uh, anyway, that, that’s enough about me. I want to hear everything about you.
I have to go to the bathroom.

I go to the bathroom, too. Sometimes more frequently than I care to admit. Oh, I’ve had it checked out, it’s nothing. Hmm. This is going great. Mmm, can I have a refill on my chai tea? Yes, I have a good feeling about this. (Girl can be seen sneaking past window and leaving) I should have bought condoms.
The apartment.

Hello, I’m Dr. Sheldon Cooper. Welcome to Sheldon Cooper Presents Fun with Flags. My apologies that this episode is coming late. I did shoot one last week, in honour of Black History Month, but I was informed by my roommate that my spot-on portrayal of George Washington Carver could be considered wildly racist. My heart goes out to the members of the African-American community, who, like me, have been kept down by The Man. Now, Fun with Flags is not just for the flag aficionado, it’s also for the flag novice, so, to help me with that, please welcome my friend, neighbour, and flag virgin, yeah, not a real virgin. She’s had coitus many times. Sometimes within earshot of this flag enthusiast. Once while he was trying to watch The Incredibles. Penny.
Hello.
So, Penny, I understand you would like to learn more about flags.
Yeah, I can’t tell you how many times I’ve been at a party where everyone’s talking about flags and I just couldn’t join in.
Yeah. Well, you came to the right place.
Uh, I’m sorry, can we just pause for a minute?
What’s wrong?
I just think it might look more natural if you talked to me instead of the camera, you know, like, like a real conversation. It’s something we work on in my acting class.
Interesting. A few people in the comments section have said that my delivery is robotic. Perhaps that isn’t the compliment it sounds like.

Yeah, let’s try it again, and maybe, this time, you could work on your body language a bit. You know, when you’re all hunched like that, you’re shutting the audience out, but when you’re relaxed and open, you’re inviting them in.
Right. And which one do I want?
Let’s try open.

If our friend, the flag, has taught me anything, it’s to go where the wind takes you. As long as you remain firmly attached to a rigid pole. And, action. So, Penny, what sort of flag questions keep you awake at night?
Um, well, I’m from Nebraska. So what can you tell me about the state flag?
Gosh, Penny, what’d you have for breakfast? A big glass of good question juice? The Nebraska state flag is simply the state seal on a field of blue. Spread your legs, invite them in.
Outside Raj’s apartment.
I’m telling you, something’s wrong. I can always feel it when Raj is in trouble.
Geez, how close were you guys before we got married?
Don’t look under that rock. (Knocking) Raj, you okay?
You in there?
Go away!
Come on, buddy, open up.
We’re worried about you.
Oh, just because I’ve stopped going to work and answering my phone you think something bad happened? Maybe something good happened.
Did something good happen?
Of course not. Nothing good ever happens. (Opens door. He is wearing a stained vest, his hair is unkempt, and he is drinking wine from a bottle.)
Whoa.
What?
Nope, just, just, whoa.
It smells pretty ripe in here. You kind feel it in your eyes.
Raj, what’s going on?
I was humiliated by yet another woman.
You didn’t kill her and chop her up, that’s not what we’re smelling, right?
No. I took her for coffee, and she snuck out the bathroom window to get away from me.
Oh, you poor baby.
I went and looked. It was a high and tiny window. She must have been very motivated.
I’m sorry. That’s awful, but come on, you got to shake it off.
Yeah, you can’t stay in your apartment for the rest of your life.
Why not? With online shopping and overnight delivery, I can get anything I want. Look, I just ordered a case of Dinty Moore beef stew and two live lobsters on Amazon.
Lobsters overnight?
Oh, you’re kidding. Let me see. Well, I’ll be. Look, you can throw in a couple steaks and have a surf and turf.
The surf and turf sounds good. See if they have corn on the cob.
Guys, we’re trying to get him out of here, not you in.
You’re wasting your time. Just please, leave me alone.
Now what?
I don’t know.
We could go to Red Lobster and talk about it. We’re all thinking it. I just had the decency to wait for him to leave.
The apartment.
Hello, Sheldon.
Hello. How’s the final stage of your nicotine addiction study going?

Fine. Just hold on. Mommy’s on the phone! Sorry. We’ve cut the monkeys down to one cigarette a day, so things are a little intense. Makes me miss my marijuana-abusing flatworms. Those guys were mellow.
Good news. Uh, the latest episode of Fun with Flags is online.
Oh, that’s right. How’d it go with Penny?
Much better than I expected. She even gave me some helpful tips about acting and body language. Watch. Welcome to my world. Not welcome to my world. Welcome. Not welcome.
Subtle, but powerful.
I know. I’m still learning to control it.
Did you tell Penny how helpful she was?
Why would I do that?
Because she’s your friend, and she did a nice job. I’m sure she’d like to hear it.
All right.
I didn’t mean now. Hello? Yeah, yeah, you want a cigarette. Well, I’d like a normal boyfriend. Deal with it.
Penny’s apartment.
Oh, hi. What’s up?
Um…
You need me to shut the door so you can do your knocking thing?
No. I didn’t start yet, it’s fine.
Okay. So, what do you need?

Well, I was thinking about you helping me out last night (knock, knock, knock) Penny. And I just wanted to tell you (knock, knock, knock) Penny, that the answer to the question, who did a great job? is you, (knock, knock, knock) Penny.
Really?
Yes, you were very natural in front of the camera, and I found your suggestions extremely helpful.
Aw, sweetie, you just made my day.
Okay.
Hey, my acting class is putting on a play Friday night. I could put you and Amy on the guest list.
Oh, that sounds terrible. Why would I want to do that?
The apartment.
That’s right. They’re no good without the lighter.
Well, so much for your advice on complimenting Penny.
Why? What happened?
She tried to rope us into going to her acting class to see a play. Don’t worry. Luckily, I had the good sense to drown that kitten in the river.
Sheldon, that’s very rude. She helped you with your show. The right thing to do is reciprocate by going to see her play.
Oh, so many crazy rules.
That better be Tootsie Rolls you’re throwing at me!
Penny’s apartment.
(Knock, knock, knock) Penny. (Knock, knock, knock) Penny. (Knock, knock, knock) Penny. Oh yeah, much better.
What?
Amy pointed out to me that since you did something nice for me, I’m obligated to do something nice for you. So, yes, I’ll go to your dopey play.
Hey, I don’t want you to go any more.
Why not?
You should go ’cause you want to go, not because you have to.
Oh, Dear Lord, more rules? Where does it stop? Can I want to go because I have to want to go?
Okay. Do whatever you want.
Yeah, but now, wait. Do whatever I want? Or whatever I have to want?
Oh, for God’s sake, just come to the play.
All right. I don’t want to, but at least that makes sense.
The comic book store.
You know, I haven’t seen Raj in several days. Is he no longer a part of our social group? And if so, should we be interviewing for a replacement? Perhaps, this time, we go Latin.
He’s just decided he’s never leaving his apartment again.
Oh, brilliant. I’ve been itching to pull that trigger.
He’s upset because he can’t get anywhere with women.
Would it help if I gave him some pointers? I’m just funnin’ ya.
Hi. I don’t know if you remember me, but I was here the other night at your party.
Oh, yeah, you left with Raj.
Uh, yeah.
You’re the one? Okay, let me tell you something. That guy you blew off happens to be my best friend. Okay? He was devastated.
Sorry. Can you just give him this?
Okay. But I gotta warn you, Raj is a proud, passionate man. If you go running out on him again, you’re only gonna get, like, three or four more chances before you are history.
Raj’s apartment.
Come on, she came back. This is good news. You should celebrate.
I don’t want to celebrate.
Not even a little? I mean, we could have a pants party. Go put some on.
Why would I want her number? I don’t want anything to do with this woman.
Oh, come on, Raj.
No, you don’t get it. I want nothing to do with any woman. My heart is stone. From now on, I’m a monk. I renounce all worldly pleasures. Except for lobster. And garlic butter.
Boy, I want to tell you it’s her loss, but you are not making it easy.
You’re, you’re a good friend for trying to help, but, I’ve made my choice.
All right. Well, I’ll see you around.
See you. No, wait, take her number. I don’t want the temptation.
Okay.
I must be strong so I don’t stray from my true purpose, the study of the universe.
All right. Thanks for ruining lobster for me.
Outside on the street.
Wait! Give me the number! Give me the number! Give me the number!
The apartment.
So, Amy, what’s going on with your addiction study?
Sadly, I’m no longer associated with that project.
Why? What happened?
Typical bureaucratic nonsense. You can get animals addicted to a harmful substance, you can dissect their brains, but you throw their own faeces back at them and suddenly you’re unprofessional.
I’m sorry. That I asked.
All right, let’s get this stupid play over with.
Uh, hang on. Empty your pockets.
Why?
You know why. The Nintendo DS. And the PSP. Now the Gameboy.
Aw, for Pete’s sake. Can we go now?
Well, is that all of it? (Pulls a Rubik’s cube from his pants.) Just set it down.
Just so you know, this is not a stupid play. A Streetcar Named Desire is an American classic.
It’s about streetcars? Oh, great. I won’t need this. (Pulls out an etch-a-sketch.)
Outside Raj’s apartment. The girl from the comic book store knocks on the door.
Just a sec. Oh, who says just a sec? I hate myself. Hello.
Hi.
Uh, would you like to come in?
Oh, no, I can’t stay.
Oh.
I just wanted to say, I’m sorry for running out of the coffee shop. That wasn’t cool. So, uh, yeah. I’m sorry.
Wait. Can you at least tell me what went wrong? It’s okay. I can take anything. Unless it’s something I did, or said, or am. ‘Cause those are, like, my buttons.
No, it’s not any of that. It’s just, I kind of have a hard time around people I don’t know.
Really? Then what were you doing at the comic book store that night?
I’ve been trying to force myself into situations that I’m not comfortable with. I saw the flyer in the store window, and I made myself go in. I don’t even like comic books.
Yeah, me neither.
Then what were you doing there?
I lied. I love them. I only said that so you’d go out with me.
Oh, you don’t want to do that. I’m kind of broken.
That’s great. I’m broken, too.
Oh, no, you’re not.

Oh, I totally am. If it wasn’t for this beer, I couldn’t even talk to you right now. I’m a wreck. There are many things seriously wrong with me. And not quirks, either. Like, diagnosable psychological problems. Maybe brain damage.
Well, how do I know you’re not just saying that?
Go out with me on one date, and I promise you, you’ll see.
Okay. Text me. Bye.
You won’t regret it. I’m the most pathetic guy you’ve ever met. And that, boys and girls, is how it’s done.
The theatre.
Yes.
I think you have a great capacity for devotion. You’ll be lonely when she passes on, won’t you? I understand what that is.
To be lonely?
She’s pretty good, huh?
She is. But when do they get to the part about streetcars?

…when I was a very young girl. When I was 16 years old, I made the discovery, love. All at once, and much, much too completely. It was like you suddenly turned a blinding light on something that had always been half a shadow. That’s how it struck the world for me. But I was unlucky. Deluded.
She’s remarkable.
She really is.
Our Penny’s a star.
How can she remember all those lines, but as a waitress, she can’t remember no tomato on my hamburger?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: No, it’s, it’s almost done. I just, I have to find the next of kin, and send ’em the DVD and then just wait for someone with my complexion to die so I can get a skin graft.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Smile.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: What is that? What is that for?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: So you can send it to Princeton and get your money back.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: The apartment.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: I must say, Sheldon, you’re handling this DVD business with an impressive amount of maturity.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: I don’t know why that surprises you. I’m a grown man. As should be evident by this sport coat and very real flower in my lapel.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Is there some kind of new coping mechanism you’re employing?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: The more interesting question you should be asking is, what does this flower smell like?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: I’m gonna go with sad. So what’s the story with you and this DVD?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: There’s nothing to tell. Maybe I purchased a book entitled Don’t Sweat the Small Stuff and I followed its wise suggestions, one of which was stop and smell the flowers.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Seriously?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Please. Ha-ha, Oh.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: A coffee shop.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Hi.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Hello. Oh, it’s so good to see you.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: You, too.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Please, sit. I, uh, I got you a cappuccino. I remembered it was your favourite. I also got crumb cake, but I remembered it was my favourite and I ate it. Anyway, uh, how are you?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: I’m pretty good. Listen, I just wanted to apologize for breaking up with you in an e-mail.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Well, and I ate all the crumb cake. We both made mistakes.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Okay.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: I’m so happy you asked me here, and I hope we can hang out again sometime. You know, as friends, lovemaking partners, whatever.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Oh, uh, I’m kind of seeing someone.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: I think I know the answer to this, but just to be clear, it’s not me, right?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Penny’s apartment.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: This is all your fault, I should’ve listened to Mun-Mun because I’ve been playing with a cobra and her name is Penny. Why are you so cruel? Do you enjoy my pain?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: There’s a girl at the Cheesecake Factory I can set you up with.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: I love you, Penny.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: The apartment.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: How is it I can conceptualize a methodology of examining dark matter in the universe but can’t figure out how to fix a novelty squirt flower?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: I think the real question is, why do you waste your time with cheap, childish pranks?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: There’s probably a deep reason. Which I’d be happy to discuss with you over some peanut brittle in a can.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Okay, Sheldon, I am out of options. Video store owner, Nursis Manookian, has no next of kin.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Well, you seem hot under the collar, or is that the sweater?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Oh, oh, no, no. It’s because I spent all afternoon at the Armenian church where his funeral mass was held. According to Father Solakian, no one attended. Luckily, my trip wasn’t a complete waste. I lit a candle and prayed for your death but I’m not Armenian, so it probably won’t work. This is over, right?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Oh, not necessarily. I suggest you look for long-lost relatives either in Armenia or Lebanon.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Listen to me, Sheldon. I am not going to Lebanon to return Super Mario Brothers the movie.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: You know, it might be fun. You love hummus.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Why isn’t this bothering you? Isn’t your brain getting itchy? This is on your card. This could be ruining your credit score. Why isn’t this making you crazy?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Leonard, I have something to tell you, but I want you to promise not to flip out.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: What?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Seven years ago, I found out the DVD was late and I paid for it.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: What?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: I was going to mention it at the time, but then I thought, some day, this might be a teachable moment.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Aaaah! I, you, how can, what!

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Sheldon, that was diabolical.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: I know. And it wasn’t easy. Do you have any idea what it’s like to wait for years and never know if you’re going to finally get satisfaction?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: A coffee shop.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Wow. You’re even prettier than Penny said. I can’t believe a girl like you doesn’t have a boyfriend.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Well, I don’t.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: I don’t believe you, you’re lying to me.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: What?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Oh, it’s okay. I have no morals and I’m desperately lonely. I’ll be the other man if you want a little something-something on the side.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: The cheesecake factory.

dialogue: What is wrong with you?

dialogue: What is wrong with you?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: Raj’s apartment.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 08 – The Itchy Brain Simulation
dialogue: What is wrong with you?
The apartment.
The math is all there. It’s not real.
Yes, it is.
Yeah,uh, look, it is scientifically impossible for a person to tip a cow. Even you, with your stocky build and lumberjack shoulders, you couldn’t do it.
It’s horrible. Why would you push a cow over? They’re sacred.
Oh, stop it. I’ve seen you eat, like, a million hamburgers.
Hey, an animal can be both sacred and delicious.
Look, I’m telling you I’ve done it, okay? I clearly remember the cow standing up and then the cow on its side.
Were you drunk?
I was 16 in Nebraska. What do you think?
I think you’re the one who fell over.
That would explain why the sky was also on its side.
Hey.
Howard. Cow tipping. Real or not?
Mmm. I’m gonna say not. That’s just based on me trying to roll my mom over when she’s snoring. Speaking of that big side of beef, uh, she’s invited all of you to Thanksgiving at her house.
Mmm. You know, I’ve been told that a bald refusal of an invitation is rude and one must instead offer up a polite excuse, so I’d love to go, but, unfortunately, that sounds awful.
Come on, it’ll be fun.
Uh, we were actually gonna do it here.
Please? Bernadette’s bringing her dad ’cause her mom’s out of town, and I never have anything to say to that guy.
Oh, since you put it that way, I’d love to go, but that sounds even more awful.
It’d actually be nice to not hear Sheldon complain about my cooking all day.
Uh, excuse me, but every year you prepare a terrible meal and every year I criticize it. Do our traditions mean nothing to you?
I want to go.
Yeah, me, too.
I’m in.
Sheldon.
Ugh, fine, I’ll go. But if her food is delicious, Thanksgiving is ruined, and it’s on you.
The apartment.
Do we really have to go to Mrs. Wolowitz’s house?
We do. And I expect you to be on your best behaviour.
Now I know how the African slaves felt. Being dragged from their homes to labour under the yoke of the white man.
Are you honestly comparing Thanksgiving dinner at Wolowitz’s mom’s with one of the greatest tragedies in the history of mankind?
Yes.
Sheldon, you can have a nice Thanksgiving anywhere. I spent one in Vegas.
You did?

Yeah, back when I was dating Zack. It was actually more fun than I thought. We gambled, we went to one of those cheesy wedding chapels, we had a really good turkey dinner. Which was surprising, since we were at a strip club.
Wait, you went to a chapel?
Yeah.
Why?
We had one of those silly fake weddings.
Penny, you know those are real, right?
No, they’re not.
Yeah, they are.
No, they’re not.
Yeah, they are.
He’s right.
They’re real.
But it didn’t seem real.
Let me ask you a question. At any point, was Las Vegas on its side?
Mrs Wolowitz’s house.
Hi, Dad.
Hi, honey.
Oh, you brought beer for everybody.
Uh, okay, yeah, it’s for everybody. I really just wanted to have a nice, quiet day at home and watch the game.
You can have a quiet day and watch the game here.
Howard, the medicine’s not working.
You just took it. At least let it reach your first stomach. (entering) Hey, Mike. Let me help you out, there.
Thanks. What’s wrong with your mom?
Oh, her gout’s flaring up. Turns out an apple pie a day does not keep the doctor away.
How can one little toe hurt so bad?
Maybe because that little piggy is being crushed by the barn. She should quiet down soon. I gave her enough pain meds to choke a, well, her.
I guess we’re gonna have to do all the cooking.
I have a better idea.
If you think you’re gonna make me do all this by myself, you’re crazy.
I was gonna make Raj do it all by himself.
Oh, well, that’s a great idea.
Leonard’s car.
No traffic, we’re sailing.
Yes. Like we’re on a ship. Coming from Africa to America.
Sheldon, that’s completely inappropriate. You can’t keep comparing yourself to a slave.
Yes, Miss Amy.
I can’t believe you’re married to that idiot.
Ugh, would you stop? We just did it as a goof.
Well, a goof or not, you’re actually married. You need to get this taken care of.
I will. Why are you making this such a big deal?
Oh, oh, oh, I have a reason. It could be because you said yes to marrying Zack, but every time Leonard’s proposed, he’s gotten a resounding no. Yeah, that’s just off the top of my head.
So how do I undo this?
I’m hoping you can get an annulment. It’s just like it never happened.
Great, well, what do I have to do?
It says here you can get an annulment if any of the following conditions are met. Were you unable to consummate the marriage?
Hah!Penny? Next.
Is there any evidence of fraud, bigamy, want of understanding?
Want of understanding? What does that even mean?
Ding, ding, ding. We have a winner.
Mrs Wolowitz’s kitchen.
Thanks for saving the day.
Ah, no problem. It wouldn’t be Thanksgiving without an Indian providing the food. Uh, now, where does your mom keep the Crisco?
Um, I don’t know. Probably in a wad in her cheek.
I’ll help Raj in here. Why don’t you go keep my dad company?
He doesn’t want me in there. I’m the creepy little guy who has sex with his daughter.
Don’t be silly, he loves you.
Does he?
Okay, he cares about you a lot.
Really?
The living room.
I do crap for you all the time. Get out there.
So your wife’s in Arizona with the grandkids?
Uh-huh.

You know, my mom’s been to Arizona. She rode one of those mules down in the Grand Canyon. Long story short, they had to shoot it. ‘Cause she’s so fat. I’ll get the door while you finish laughing. Hey, guys.
Happy Thanksgiving.
It smells wonderful. Is anyone slaving away in the kitchen? Because I, too, know…
Sheldon.
Here. Thank you for having us.
What’s with you?
Oh, she’s mad at me because she just found out she’s married to Zack.
Really? That dumb-ass she used to date? That’s hysterical.
I can’t believe I felt bad for opening this in the car.
The kitchen.
You need any help?
Uh, yeah, can you, uh, reach that, uh, gravy boat up there?
Uh, sure.

Great. That makes one of you. Okay, we have a lot to do and not much time to do it. Bernadette, you’re on corn, gravy and yam detail. Amy, you’re on rolls, cranberries and making sure Bernadette stays away from the marshmallows. That’s right, I see you. Okay, if you have any questions, I’ll be over here basting my ass off. Focus is key.
Did you guys know Penny married Zack three years ago?
What?
The living room.
You ever play football?
A little in college. You?
No. But I did get tackled in the hallway once. The whole school cheered.
Okay, I found the, uh, court papers that you and Zack need to fill out. I’ll print them when we get home.
Fine.
And we can just put this whole thing behind us.
Are you done?
What?
Look, I get it, I screwed up. Is this all we’re gonna talk about the rest of the day?
Why are you mad at me? You’re the one that did the stupid thing. I’m just trying to fix it.
Ugh, I need some air.
Wuh, Penny.
I don’t know the first thing about women, but I would not follow her.
Listen to Stretch.
How am I the bad guy? She’s the one who married someone else. I’m the victim.
Sounds like Zack’s the victim. You’re sleeping with his wife.
I’ve kept my marriage together for 35 years. Can I weigh in here?
Sure.
I’m trying to watch the game. Shut up. Oh, how do you not make a first down there?
They passed against a nickel defence. They should have run it off-tackle.
How the hell do you know that?
My father loved football. He always made me watch it before I was allowed to do my homework.
Well, you’ll be happy to know I just spoke to Zack and he’s willing to sign the court papers. He’s on his way here now.
Wait, you invited him here?
Yeah.
I’m getting ready to weigh in again.
Come on.
What do you think they ought to do now?
I would throw a quick slant to a wideout, given that the defence is showing blitz.
Oh, I love a good blitz, especially with sour cream. Get it? ‘Cause it sounds like blintz.
Did someone say blintz?
The dining room.
I just don’t understand why you invited him here today.
Because you wouldn’t shut up about it. When I called him, he had nothing to do, so I just thought it would…
Hey, guys, I’m trying to cook in here.
Oh, sorry. We’ll keep it down.
No, no, speak up. I’m about to use the blender, and I don’t want to miss anything.
Well, you might have to cook for one more because she invited Zack.
What?
Ooh!
My, my. The plot, like my gravy, thickens.
The living room.
I don’t care for your mother’s bathroom. There’s not an angle to do one’s business without a clown figurine staring at you.
That’s why I sit.
Yeah, that’s why. You remember the Thanksgiving game when it snowed in Dallas?
1993. Leon Lett blew the game in the final seconds and the Dolphins emerged victorious. Then I finally got to do my calculus.
I was so pissed, I wanted to shoot my TV.
So was my dad. And then he did.
Anyone need a beer?
Yeah.
Thank God.
So, does your dad still live in Texas?
No. He died when I was 14.
I’m sorry to hear that.
So was the man who owned the local liquor store. He cried and cried.
Here you go.
Oh, thanks. So, if your dad died when you were 14, you were never old enough to have a beer with the man.
No, sir. He did try to give me one for my high school graduation, but I was 11 and my mom said no.
Well, you’re having one with me.
All right.
To your dad.
I never had a beer with my dad, either.
Do you mind? We’re having a moment here.
The kitchen.
I can’t believe Penny’s married to Zack.
Wonder what she saw in that guy.
I don’t know. He’s sweet, he’s tall, handsome.
Broad shoulders, good hair.
Hmm. Wonder what she sees in Leonard.
How’s it going out there?
Sheldon and your dad are bonding and completely ignoring me.
I know how you feel. Sheldon ignored me for a week when he got that Roomba vacuum. I kick it when he’s not looking.
What are they doing?
They’re drinking beer and watching football.
So why don’t you do that with them?
They don’t want me.
What do you mean?
Well, Sheldon started talking about how his dad isn’t alive any more, and they were toasting, and I tried to tell them about how sad I was when my dad abandoned…
Zack’s here!
Stir the gravy.
Sorry. I really want to hear how sad you are. I’ll be back in like five, ten minutes.
The dining room.
Sorry she made you come over here on a holiday.
It’s all right. I didn’t have anything going on. Plus, Penny told me we’re married, and Thanksgiving’s a time to be with family.
Yeah, okay, great. Can we just get this over with?
Yeah, uh, you guys have to sign here and here. On Monday, we’ll file for the annulment, and this marriage will be over.
Okay.
I don’t know if I want to sign it.
Ooh.
Why won’t you sign it?
I just think splitting up can be rough on kids.
We don’t have any kids.
Are you sure? ‘Cause you didn’t know we were married until this morning.
Okay, look, Zack, come on. You know neither of us thought this was real. I mean, we were married by an Elvis impersonator.
Of course it was an impersonator. We could never afford a real Elvis.
You married him instead of me? Good call. Sign the papers.
Hang on. You know what? You have been a jerk about this all day. You always do this, whenever I mess up, you’re right there to make me feel even worse about it.
That is not true.
Yeah, we could’ve waited till Monday, signed the papers, this all would have been over.
You’re the one who invited him here.
Oh, there you go again, just another mistake you’re throwing in my face.
Not cool, bro. I’m starting to think you’re not the kind of guy I want dating my wife.
Yeah, well, she’s not gonna be your wife for long.
Oh, no. Are you dying?
I’m about to. Sign the paper.
Know what they say, happy wife, happy life. Let’s eat.
The living room.
Two, three, eight, four, six. (Normal) That’s all I can do without throwing up.
That is not what I expected when you said you were gonna burp pie.
Did somebody say pie?
I don’t know what’s scarier, the bathroom clowns or the woman that put them there.

All I know is you can only fit one of her in a car. And there’s the clown that came out of her. I really didn’t want to come here, but this is shaping up to be one of the best Thanksgivings I’ve had in a long time.
Me, too.
Hey. Howie says you’ve been making fun of him all day. Now, both of you apologize right now.
She’s so tiny. It’s funny when she’s mad.
All right, mister, I think you owe Howard and Bernadette an apology.
Perhaps you’re right. I’m sorry for my behaviour. I’ve had alcohol, and it’s caused me to be inappropriate.
It’s okay.
Don’t worry about it.
Thank you.
Ain’t she great?
Mmm.
Sheldon.
Now, how’s about you get us a couple of beers?
The dining room.
Thanks again for cooking.
Yeah, everything was delicious.
Well, I couldn’t have done it without my two favourite girls. Martha Stewart and Rachael Ray.
Hey, Sheldon, what do you say we go outside and throw around the old pigskin?
This is a Jewish house. I don’t think they have pigskin.
Did someone say pigskin?
Hey, I’m sorry about today. And I promise, next time I get married, it won’t be a joke. It’ll be for love. Or money.
I’m sorry, too.
Don’t be. It’s my fault. I was a terrible husband. I was never around.
I know I’m hard on you, but you’re not the worst son-in-law in the world.
Mike, that’s the nicest thing you’ve ever said to me.
Well, I’m drunk.
I just vomited on a lot of clowns.
A radio studio.
This is Science Friday. I’m Ira Flatow. My guest today is responsible for the discovery of the first stable super-heavy element. Welcome, Dr. Sheldon Cooper.
Thank you. Uh, the university made me come here. I didn’t want to. Uh, big fan of the show.
So, I understand that you actually discovered this element by mistake.
Yes.
And some people in the science community are calling it The Wonder Blunder.
Who? Give me their names. I bet it’s Wolowitz.
It’s just such a fascinating story. Your calculations are way off, but they find the element anyway. It’s like misreading a treasure map and still finding the treasure.
Can we talk about something else? Do you know that I yodel?
That’s interesting, but this could be taking you down the path toward a Nobel Prize. And in chemistry, no less. And wouldn’t that be unusual? Because you’re a physicist.

Yes, yes, I’d be a physicist with a Nobel in chemistry. Everyone laugh at the circus freak. You know, I don’t need to sit here and take this, Flatow. It is because of bullies like you, every day more and more Americans are making the switch to television.
The apartment. Sheldon is on the phone.

President Seibert, I don’t know why you’re yelling. You’re the one who made me go on the radio. I was expecting a professional science interview, not an attack by some morning zoo shock jock. Well, if the university needs money so badly, perhaps you should start a swear jar. Whoa, that one’s worth a dollar.
I know you don’t like it, but every time you do an interview, it raises the profile of the university. That translates to funding.
Yeah, well, I’m not just some trained monkey dancing for coins.
Of course you’re not. People love trained monkeys.
How can you not be happy? You’re tall, thin and famous. Oh, my God, I’m jealous of Sheldon.
Look, you’re gonna be doing this stuff for a while. You’re just gonna have to find a way to get used to it.
But none of you know what this is like. Being celebrated for something you wish you never did.
Mmm, you clearly haven’t been with me at Mardi Gras.
Howard and Bernadette’s apartment.
Want to pause the video game and help me clean up?
I am cleaning up. Look at the mess the Joker made of Gotham City.
Come on, it’s your friend who’s coming to stay here.
Raj grew up in India. Trust me, he’s seen worse.
Howie.
I promise I’ll help out the rest of the week.
The rest of the week? You said it was just gonna be a night or two.
Yeah, but if I told you a week, would you have said yes?
No.
Then you left me no choice.
I love Raj, but that’s a long time for a house guest.
I know, but they’re tenting his building. He can’t find a hotel he likes that allows dogs.
He’s bringing Cinnamon?
For a whole week, the nerve of some people.
Sheldon’s bedroom. Sheldon is playing with his train set.
Here comes the Embarrassment Express. With stops at Fraudville, Wonder Blunderberg, and Kansas City. Because it’s a hub.
Sheldon, can I come in?
Do you have cookies?
No.
Good. I don’t deserve cookies. Come in. Wil?
Hey, Sheldon. It’s been a while.
Why are you here?
Amy said you were having a rough time, and I thought maybe we could talk. Is that okay?
Certainly. Although, right now, I’m having a rough time because there’s three people in my room, and it’s starting to feel like a discotheque.
Sheldon, you said you were unhappy getting attention for something you wished you never did.
Yeah, I know a little something about that.
Oh, nonsense, Wil. Your endless tweets are not that bad.
I remember why it’s been a while. Sheldon, I was actually talking about when I was a kid on Star Trek.
How could you not like getting attention for playing Wesley Crusher? You were wonderful. A know-it-all boy genius with an eidetic memory. Who couldn’t relate to that?
Well, not everybody felt that way. A lot of people really hated the character, and some of them hated me because of it. I would do interviews, and people would be mean to me.
That just happened to me. Next time you’re stuck for a tweet, feel free to say what a jerk Ira Flatow is.
Sheldon, the point is Wil learned to embrace that part of his life and moved on to bigger and better things.
Yeah, I’m an author now, I do public speaking, and I have my own Web series about board games.
Uh, we’re trying to cheer him up, so…

I’m just saying that there was a time when I thought I would never get out of Wesley Crusher’s shadow. But now, it’s just one small part of a pretty great life, and it’s a part that I’m happy is there.
I do see what you’re saying. That helps.
Good.
Would you two like to stay and play trains with me?
Sure.
Okay.
Oh, great, now, I work the controls, I say all aboard. You sit quietly and watch.
Can I blow the whistle?
You should probably go.
Howard and Bernadette’s apartment.
You’re gonna brush your teeth on my couch?
No, I’m gonna brush Cinnamon’s teeth.
Why bother? She spends half the time licking her butt.
And the other half licking my face. That’s why I’m brushing her teeth.
Hey, guys. Sorry I’m so late. Did you already have dinner?
No, we were waiting for you.
Aw, that’s so sweet.
Yeah. So what do you feel like making?
Howard, the poor thing just got home from work. Let me get you a glass of wine. I’ll cook dinner.
Oh, Raj, you’re our guest.

dialogue: The apartment.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: What you working on?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I’m writing an appeal to the Faculty Senate, so that I can move on from string theory.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Oh. How’s it going?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: You tell me. Dear Esteemed Colleagues, as you may know, I have requested to change my field of study. My decision to do so is, I believe, in the best interest of science. At your convenience, I’d be happy to explain it to you in words you’ll understand.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: It’s nice that you called them esteemed.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: You’re right. I’ll take that out.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: So, listen, there was something I was hoping to float past you.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Mm.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Now that Penny and I are engaged, I thought we might want to talk about our living arrangements.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Of course. She’s spent many nights here, and you’re worried about preserving the myth of her virginity before the wedding.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I’m not.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Good, because not only has that ship sailed, if it hit an iceberg, countless men would perish.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Actually, this is about where she and I are going to live.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: What do you mean?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Well, well, we might want to live together.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Oh, yeah, well, I’ve already given this some thought, and I’m willing to let Penny live with us one day a week for a trial period. Now, obviously, not when she’s made cranky by the shedding of her uterine lining.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: That’s very sweet. But we were thinking more of us maybe living together with… not you.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I don’t understand. How could we all live together if I’m not there?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Look, I, I know this is, this is change, and that sounds scary.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Where are you going to go?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I don’t know. We just started to think about this. Maybe I’ll move in with Penny, or maybe she and I’ll take this place, and you can move across the hall.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Move across the hall? Did you take a marijuana?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: No, I did not.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Did you get hit on the head with a coconut?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: No.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Well, then, I’m all out of guesses. What? Me move across the hall. Why would you even suggest such a thing?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Because I love Penny, and want to give her the life she deserves.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I see. You’re putting your future bride’s happiness above mine.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Well, yeah.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Wow.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Amy’s apartment.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: How dare the university force me to go back to string theory?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: They just don’t appreciate you.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Yeah, and on top of that, Leonard has the audacity to suggest that now that he and Penny are engaged, he may not want to live with me any more.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Here, I made you some Strawberry Quik.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I have real problems here, Amy. I can’t be mollified with a beverage designed for children. Mmm, yummy.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: You know, this might work out for the best. I mean, you’re always complaining about what a terrible roommate Leonard is. Like how he turns up the thermostat when you’re not there.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Ugh, it’s like walking into the Amazon. And not the good Amazon with one-day shipping. The awful one with birds and snakes.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: You hate the sound of all those keys on his key chain.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Four keys! Who does he think he is, a warden?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: See? Maybe you’ll love living alone.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I don’t know. Perhaps.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: And if it turns out you don’t, you and I could live together.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: You and… oh, sure, and while we’re at it, why don’t we get engaged, too? Why don’t we get a little house, start a family? Enjoy our sunset years together? Do you hear yourself, woman?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Sheldon, it was just a thought.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: No. Here’s a thought. You’re not moving in, Leonard’s not moving out, everything stays exactly the way it is. And by the way, I saw you make this Strawberry Quik with syrup, you’re supposed to use the powder.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: It tastes the same.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: No. The syrup tastes better and I don’t like it.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: The apartment.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: This is so sweet. You never cook for me.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Well, you cook for me all the time and, ugh.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: If you don’t like my cooking, why haven’t you ever said anything?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: It’s hard to talk with so much heavy chewing to do.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Sorry. I’ll get better.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I know you’ll try. So, should we talk about setting a date?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Well, I’d like to pick one that works with my brother’s schedule.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Okay. And when would that be?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Uh, 12 to 18 months from now, depending on good behaviour.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Hi, is Sheldon here?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: No, I thought he was with you.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: He was, but he stormed off and now he isn’t answering his phone.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: What happened?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: He was really angry that you suggested he move out.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Oh.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I also mentioned that he and I could live together but he was too mad at you to realize what a great idea that is.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Well, he’s been having a couple of tough days. I’m sure he’s fine. He probably just needs a little alone time to decompress.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: You’re probably right. So, what are you guys doing?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Well, Leonard cooked for me and now we’re just having a nice dinner, you know, as a newly engaged couple.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: That’s nice.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Anyway, as I was saying, Sheldon probably just needs a little alone time. ‘Cause that’s important. Not just for him, but for most anybody, really.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Don’t I know it. What is that, polenta?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Amy, get out.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Right.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: The comic book store.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: No.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Hey, Sheldon.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: What happened?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I was cooking in the back room last night and the hot plate caught on fire.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: And you couldn’t put it out?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I was across the street at the do-it-yourself car wash, taking a shower.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: So when will you reopen?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Um, I don’t know. I’m waiting to hear back from the insurance company.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: So, tomorrow?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I don’t mean to be rude, Sheldon, but, uh, my life is kind of falling apart right now.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Your life? The university is making me do string theory and my girlfriend loves me so much she wants to live with me. And now, the place I need to go when I’m sad is damp and smells funny.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Well, sorry I let you down.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: No. I do not accept this. Everything is changing and I hate it. It stops now. I’m helping you get back on your feet. I would like to purchase this comic book, please.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: That’ll be $2.99.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Really? It’s soaking wet.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Fine, a dollar.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Can you break a twenty?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: No, I only have hundreds.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: You know what? I don’t always recognize sarcasm, but I do right now, and I don’t appreciate it. I’m sorry for your loss. But you’re not the only one whose day has been a disaster.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: (Light falls on ground just where he was standing a moment before) That could have killed me. I can’t catch a break.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: The apartment.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I haven’t heard from Sheldon in a while. You think he’s okay?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Oh, I’m sure he’s fine.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I’m gonna see where he is.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: How?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Oh, I know his password, so I can track his phone.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: You do that?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Not always, but ever since he wandered off at the swap meet chasing a balloon, I get worried.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: He can take care of himself. Look, we went over stranger danger and gave him that whistle.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: That’s weird.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: What?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: He’s at the train station.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: So? He loves trains.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: It’s dark out and he’s alone, I don’t like it. Let’s go get him.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: It’s sweet how you look out for him. You’re a good guy.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: It’s not just that. My mother would kill me if I let something happen to him.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: The comic book store.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Dude, I’m so sorry.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Don’t take this the wrong way, but did you do this for the insurance money?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: No. God, you sound like the police, the firemen, my parents, my therapist and the insurance company.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: We’re here for you, man. Whatever you need, okay?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Uh, actually, I was wondering if I could crash at your place for a few nights.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Sure, of course. Oh, actually, Emily was gonna spend the night.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: You slept with her? Nice.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Well, I can’t take all the credit. She let me do it to her, but, uh, but I can always call her and cancel.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Hang on. I know a place you can stay and earn some money at the same time.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Great.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I just have to warn you, it’ll involve humiliation, degradation and verbal abuse.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: So what’s the catch?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: The train station.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Sheldon.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: You tracked my phone?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Yeah.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Boy, you chase one balloon for three miles.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: We were worried about you.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Don’t be melodramatic. I’m just getting on a train and leaving forever.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Seriously? You don’t even have a change of clothes or a toothbrush.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: My plan is to stop at malls and buy what I need. It’s called living off the land.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Okay, I know you’re upset and there’s a lot of stuff going on, but it’s nothing we can’t work out. Come on, let’s get you home.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: No. I’ve reached my breaking point. I need to leave. Now.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: And go where?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: It doesn’t matter.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: So a few things don’t go your way and your best decision is to ride the rails like a hobo?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I suppose it is. Except I have a credit card. And I refuse to carry my laptop at the end of a stick. And I’d sooner die than eat beans out of a can.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Come on, come home with us and tomorrow I’ll, I’ll take you to Legoland.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Legoland is not the solution to everything. And it’s too much of a scene since that movie came out.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Then what can I do?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Leonard, I am overwhelmed. Everything is changing and it’s simply too much. I need to get away and think.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Oh, come on, you know you’re overreacting.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Leonard, hang on. Just come here. Maybe we need to let him go.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: What? Why?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: It might be good for him.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: You know he can’t take a trip like this by himself.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: He’s a grown man.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: No, he looks like a grown man. You’ve seen Freaky Friday, sometimes little kids end up in big person bodies.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Leonard, we can’t protect him forever.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I know, but…

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: He’ll be okay. You taught him well, Padawan.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Good Lord. Padawan’s the student, not the teacher.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Seriously, let him go.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Sheldon, if you really need to do this, I’m not gonna stand in your way.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I do.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Okay. Good luck.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Be safe and call us.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I will.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Bye, buddy. Sheldon?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Yes?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I’m gonna miss you.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Of course you are.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: He just made that easier.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Mm.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Mrs Wolowitz’s house.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Hey. What are you guys still doing here? I got this, go. Go home.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: You sure?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Yeah, she’s fed, she took her pills, she’s all tucked in and watching TV.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: So, she’s not too much for you?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Are you kidding? I love her, she’s great.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Stewie, you gonna watch Wheel of Fortune with me?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Coming, Debbie.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: You call her Debbie?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: She insisted. So, hey, guys, thank you so much. This job is a dream come true.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Was that a little weird?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Yeah. I don’t know why, but something about it feels unnatural.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Okay, let’s go.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Yep.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: The apartment.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Okay, Sheldon, thanks for checking in. Talk to you tomorrow? Oh, okay, bye.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: He’s okay?

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Actually sounds like he’s doing pretty well.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: I really think this is gonna be for the best.

episode_name: Series 07 Episode 24 – The Status Quo Combustion
dialogue: Me, too. And he was able to take a sabbatical from…

dialogue: Are you sure?

dialogue: Boy, I just can’t seem to get these scissors back together. Can you do it?

dialogue: Okay, that’s great. Now, let it go.

dialogue: Why would she even do this?

dialogue: Make this interesting? You bet money on me?

episode_name: Series 08 Episode 15 – The Comic Book Store Regeneration

dialogue: I think I left my pen in there.

dialogue: The comic book store.

dialogue: I understand why you’re upset, but he worked really hard to get the store ready. And it’s just furniture.

episode_name: Series 08 Episode 15 – The Comic Book Store Regeneration
dialogue: It’s my mom’s furniture. It belongs in the house I grew up in, next to that pile of TV Guides and in plain view of what, for a ten-year-old, was a quality piece of string art.

dialogue: This is why I had to rewrite our wedding vows.

dialogue: Dude, I, I think that’s Nathan Fillion.

episode_name: Series 08 Episode 15 – The Comic Book Store Regeneration
dialogue: I’m sorry, but it’s making me crazy.

dialogue: Can you please just let it go?

dialogue: What’s wrong?

dialogue: Uh, that was my aunt. Ma took a nap. She never woke up.

episode_name: Series 08 Episode 15 – The Comic Book Store Regeneration
dialogue: Oh, my God, Howie.

episode_name: Series 08 Episode 15 – The Comic Book Store Regeneration

episode_name: Series 08 Episode 15 – The Comic Book Store Regeneration
dialogue: I don’t know.

episode_name: Series 08 Episode 15 – The Comic Book Store Regeneration
dialogue: Not right now, Sheldon.

episode_name: Series 08 Episode 15 – The Comic Book Store Regeneration
dialogue: But I think it would be comforting.

episode_name: Series 08 Episode 15 – The Comic Book Store Regeneration
dialogue: Buddy.

episode_name: Series 08 Episode 15 – The Comic Book Store Regeneration
dialogue: No, it’s okay. What?

dialogue: I really thought he was gonna say let it go.
